data.title: Lumon Terminal Pro
data.author: jervant
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了苹果原创剧集《Severance》的编辑过程，特别是在Mac上进行的剪辑工作。文章还提到观众可以观看该剧集，并且购买新Mac的用户可以免费获得三个月Apple TV+的订阅服务。此外，文章包含剧透提醒，并附有购买Mac的链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕科技产品、影视元素及相关文化现象的评论

不同观点：
• [kps] 指出展示的设备是1977年推出的Data General 6053终端，并将其与同年发布的Apple II进行对比，突显其历史和技术背景。
• [fathermarz] 质疑Mac Studio的目标受众，认为在Mac Mini、iMac和MacBook Pro已经能够处理复杂工作流的情况下，Mac Studio的定位显得不明朗。
• [joeblubaugh] 对Lumon字体表示兴趣，询问其具体名称，显示出对设计和字体细节的关注。
• [WorldPeas] 表达了对未来50周年版Mac的期待，希望它能继承当前展示产品的一些时尚元素（"swag"）。
• [nasretdinov] 以幽默的方式提到因误解指示而购买了不必要的东西，反映出对产品或广告吸引力的调侃。

补充讨论：
• [ndegruchy] 表达了对某款键盘的强烈渴望，可能与展示的复古或特定风格键盘有关。
• [Clamchop] 简单评价工作内容“神秘且重要”，未明确具体内容，但表现出一定的认同态度。
• [voidwtf] 表示自己几乎毫不犹豫地准备购买产品，暗示对产品的强烈购买欲。
• [tonyedgecombe] 提到视频中未提及Mac Pro或Mac Studio，仅使用Mac mini、iMac和MacBook Pro进行剪辑工作，质疑Mac Studio的实际需求。
• [tylerflick] 指出页面在iPhone 13的Safari浏览器中无法正确显示，特别指出在竖屏模式下的问题，关注技术实现和兼容性。
• [novoreorx] 认为展示的设备只是普通的Cyberdeck，并提到其他更酷的例子（提供链接），对当前展示设备表示不以为然。
• [MaxGripe] 提出DaVinci Resolve软件比展示中使用的工具更好，隐含对工具选择的个人偏好。
• [Apocryphon] 认为展示的设备至少比Cardiff Electric Giant要好，带有比较意味。
• [piyuv] 通过对比Lumon公司（影视作品中的虚构邪恶公司）与Apple，讽刺人们对Apple产品的盲目喜爱，揭示影视对现实消费行为的影响。

争议焦点：
• 对Mac Studio实际需求和目标受众的质疑（fathermarz, tonyedgecombe）。
• 对展示设备独特性和价值的不同看法（novoreorx, Apocryphon, kps）。
• 对Apple产品和影视作品中公司形象的讽刺性对比，揭示消费文化的盲目性（piyuv）。

data.title: Blasting Past WebP - An analysis of the NSO BLASTPASS iMessage exploit
data.author: el_duderino
data.article_summary: 本文分析了NSO集团利用的iMessage零点击漏洞（BLASTPASS）。2023年9月7日，Apple发布iOS安全更新，修复了两个被活跃利用的漏洞（CVE），这些漏洞由NSO集团的零点击漏洞利用程序引发，目标是一名在国际非政府组织工作的个人。该漏洞通过恶意PassKit附件，利用iMessage发送恶意图片，无需用户交互即可入侵运行iOS 16.6的iPhone。此前，Apple已向WebP项目报告该漏洞，并在随后发布修复。Google也在Chrome中修复了此问题。尽管Isosceles和Dark Navy博客详细分析了WebP漏洞的技术细节，但未解密如何在零点击场景中实现一键利用。本文作者Ian Beer通过与Amnesty International Security Lab合作，获取了BLASTPASS样本文件和崩溃日志，揭示了NSO如何实现零点击iOS漏洞利用。漏洞核心在于WebP解码过程中的Huffman编码处理不当，导致内存损坏，尽管问题触发后解析停止，但攻击者仍能利用此缺陷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对NSO Group复杂的0-click漏洞利用技术的分析及安全对策讨论

不同观点：
• **对技术复杂性的赞赏**：
  - nneonneo指出，该漏洞利用涉及多个复杂技巧，包括使用多种图像文件格式、堆块对齐、反序列化巨大对象图、绕过PAC等。这些技巧大多是非公开的，显示出NSO团队在漏洞研究上投入了大量时间和精力。尽管其行为不当（如监视记者），但技术复杂度和持久性令人印象深刻。
  
• **对NSO Group行为的道德批判与开放源代码的呼吁**：
  - botanical将NSO Group称为“雇佣的恐怖组织”，指出其0-click漏洞被用于针对民间社会，任何人都可以付费用于监视记者、非政府组织和政客。主张开放源代码是保障安全的关键。

• **对Apple产品安全性的改进建议**：
  - nxobject建议Apple应通过影响用户体验（UX）的方式来缓解附件漏洞，例如不渲染消息预览或默认禁用某些文件格式。考虑到Apple的隐私保护形象，用户可能愿意为安全牺牲一些UX。
  - danilonc询问Lockdown Mode是否能缓解此漏洞链的部分攻击，并引用Apple支持页面说明Lockdown Mode阻挡大多数附件类型。
  - TheDong认为iMessage接收来自陌生人的消息并处理附件是不合理的，建议添加“仅接收联系人消息”的设置，类似于Signal的消息请求功能，以提高安全性。

• **技术细节的补充与具体例子的分享**：
  - qingcharles提到更改文件扩展名以绕过检查的技巧在许多网站上有效，并分享了具体例子，如将.gif文件重命名为.jpg以绕过上传限制。
  - bawolff对Google Project Zero的分析表示赞赏，并幽默地评论了PKPass格式的规范问题。
  
• **对漏洞利用的政治性评论**：
  - ipython讽刺性地指出，此类漏洞也可以用于针对美国国家安全机构，暗示即使是高安全性的机构也可能受到影响。

补充讨论：
• **编程语言安全的讨论**：
  - cedws认为内存不安全语言不适合用于此类目的，主张替换为更安全的语言。
  
• **技术文档的更新信息**：
  - lukeh提到更新的CF版本已作为swift-corelibs-foundation的一部分提供。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于如何在保障用户体验的同时提升安全性，特别是在iMessage等即时通讯工具中如何有效防止0-click漏洞攻击。NSO Group的技术复杂性令人印象深刻，但其行为的道德性和合法性备受质疑，推动了对安全措施和开放源代码的讨论。

43493056.article_content:
An analysis of the NSO BLASTPASS iMessage exploit
Posted by Ian Beer, Google Project Zero
On September 7, 2023 Apple
issued
an out-of-band security update for iOS:
Around the same time on September 7th 2023,
Citizen Lab published a blog post
linking the two CVEs fixed in iOS 16.6.1 to an "NSO Group Zero-Click, Zero-Day exploit captured in the wild":
"
[The target was] an individual employed by a Washington DC-based civil society organization with international offices...
The exploit chain was capable of compromising iPhones running the latest version of iOS (16.6) without any interaction from the victim.
The exploit involved PassKit attachments containing malicious images sent from an attacker iMessage account to the victim."
The day before, on September 6th 2023, Apple
reported a vulnerability to the WebP project
, indicating in the report that they planned to ship a custom fix for Apple customers the next day.
The WebP team posted their first
proposed fix
in the public git repo the next day, and five days after that on September 12th Google released a
new Chrome stable release
containing the WebP fix. Both Apple and Google marked the issue as exploited in the wild, alerting other integrators of WebP that they should rapidly integrate the fix as well as causing the security research community to take a closer look...
A couple of weeks later on September 21st 2023, former Project Zero team lead Ben Hawkes (in collaboration with
@mistymntncop
) published the
first detailed writeup
of the root cause of the vulnerability on the
Isosceles
Blog. A couple of months later, on November 3rd, a group called
Dark Navy
published their first blog post: a two-part analysis (
Part 1
-
Part 2
) of the WebP vulnerability and a
proof-of-concept exploit
targeting Chrome (CVE-2023-4863).
Whilst the Isosceles and Dark Navy posts explained the underlying memory corruption vulnerability in great detail, they were unable to solve another fascinating part of the puzzle: just how exactly do you land an exploit for this vulnerability in a one-shot, zero-click setup? As we'll soon see, the corruption primitive is very limited. Without access to the samples it was almost impossible to know.
In mid-November, in collaboration with
Amnesty International Security Lab
, I was able to obtain a number of BLASTPASS
PKPass
sample files as well as crash logs from failed exploit attempts.
This blog post covers my analysis of those samples and the journey to figure out how one of NSO's recent zero-click iOS exploits really worked. For me that journey began by immediately taking three months of paternity leave, and resumed in March 2024 where this story begins:
Setting the scene
For a detailed analysis of the root-cause of the WebP vulnerability and the primitive it yields, I recommend first reading the three blog posts I mentioned earlier (
Isosceles
,
Dark Navy 1
,
Dark Navy 2
.) I won't restate their analyses here (both because you should read their original work, and because it's quite complicated!) Instead I'll briefly discuss WebP and the corruption
primitive the vulnerability
yields.
WebP
WebP
is a relatively modern image file format, first released in 2010. In reality WebP is actually two completely distinct image formats:
a lossy format
based on the VP8 video codec and a separate
lossless format
. The two formats share nothing apart from both using a
RIFF
container and the string
WEBP
for the first chunk name. From that point on (12 bytes into the file) they are completely different. The vulnerability is in the lossless format, with the RIFF chunk name
VP8L
.
Lossless WebP makes extensive use of
Huffman coding
; there are at least 10 huffman trees present in the BLASTPASS sample. In the file they're stored as
canonical huffman trees
, meaning that only the code lengths are retained. At decompression time those lengths are converted directly into a two-level huffman decoding table, with the five largest tables all getting squeezed together into the same pre-allocated buffer. The (it turns out not quite) maximum size of these tables is pre-computed based on the number of symbols they encode. If you're up to this part and you're slightly lost, the other three blogposts referenced above explain this in detail.
With control over the symbol lengths it's possible to define all sorts of strange trees, many of which aren't valid. The fundamental issue was that the WebP code only checked the validity of the tree
after
building the decoding table. But the pre-computed size of the decoding table was only correct for
valid
trees.
As the Isosceles blog post points out, this means that a fundamental part of the vulnerability is that triggering the bug
is
detected, though after memory has been corrupted, and image parsing stops only a few lines of code later
. This presents another exploitation mystery: in a zero-click context, how do you exploit a bug where every time the issue is triggered it also stops parsing any attacker-controlled data?
The second m

data.title: What went wrong with the Alan Turing Institute?
data.author: alexicon
data.article_summary: 《如何不建立一个AI研究所：艾伦·图灵研究所的失败》一文揭示了英国国家AI研究所面临的危机。尽管2024年获得了1亿英镑的新 funding，艾伦·图灵研究所（ATI）仍计划大规模裁员并削减四分之一的研究项目，员工公开反抗。尽管2023年生成式AI热潮席卷全球，ATI却未能引领潮流，反而处于防御状态。批评指出，ATI未能在AI关键进展如大型语言模型（LLM）和通用人工智能（AGI）上发挥预期作用。英国研究与创新机构对ATI的审查也对其治理和财务管理提出批评。文章分析了ATI失败的原因，包括创建时目标模糊、过度依赖大学合作以及未能适应AI快速发展。尽管投入超过2.5亿英镑，ATI仍未能实现其预期目的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国图灵人工智能研究所（ATI）的资金、管理和成效问题

不同观点：
• **批评图灵研究所的资金分配和管理问题**：[smallpipe] 指出，Matt Clifford 通过图灵研究所为其在Entrepreneur First的伙伴获取资金，且未披露利益冲突。评论质疑政府为何允许这种情况发生，并对研究所的管理和独立性表示怀疑。
• **英国AI领域缺乏吸引力**：[greatgib] 认为英国在AI领域的影响力减弱，部分原因是软件工程师和研究人员的薪资缺乏吸引力，导致难以吸引国际人才。评论提到英国职位的薪资水平较低，与欧洲其他地区相比缺乏竞争力。
• **大学与科技公司之间的对比**：[snickmy] 认为，大学在吸引顶尖AI人才方面不如大科技公司，因为大学缺乏实际执行经验，且受制于官僚主义和分散的领导。评论强调大学环境与科技公司的执行力差距，以及政府资助项目的分散性。
• **对图灵研究所的不知情与质疑**：[hermitcrab] 表示作为英国软件工程师对图灵研究所知之甚少，质疑其是否产生有意义的成果，并批评电影《模仿游戏》对Alan Turing的处理。

Introduction
The UK’s national AI institute is in crisis. Despite
receiving
a fresh £100 million funding settlement in 2024, the Alan Turing Institute (ATI) is gearing up for mass redundancies and
to cut a quarter of its research projects
. Staff are in
open revolt
.
In 2023, when generative AI fever swept the world, far from taking centre stage, the ATI found itself playing defence. A report from the Tony Blair Institute
argued that
:
While industry figures have predicted some advances and privately warned of major risks, existing government channels have failed to anticipate the trajectory of progress. For example, neither the key advance of transformers nor its application in LLMs were picked up by advisory mechanisms until ChatGPT was headline news. Even the most recent AI strategies of the Alan Turing Institute, University of Cambridge and UK government make little to no mention of AGI, LLMs or similar issues.
Martin Goodson, then of the Royal Statistical Society,
dubbed
the ATI
“at best irrelevant to the development of modern AI in the UK”
.
The criticism hasn’t slowed. Matt Clifford’s
AI Opportunities Action Plan
recommended that the government should
“consider the broad institutional landscape and the full potential of the Alan Turing Institute to drive progress at the cutting edge”
. While Clifford was too diplomatic to say the quiet bit out loud, in government speak, this is code for suggesting that the ATI was not fulfilling its intended purpose.
UK Research and Innovation, the UK’s main research and innovation funding body, is running out of patience. Its
quinquennial review of the ATI
, published in 2024, was politely scathing about the institute’s governance, financial management, and the quality of its most recent strategy (dubbed Turing 2.0).
There aren’t many areas of consensus across the UK’s fractious tech community, but the ATI has come to play an oddly unifying role. From left to right and north to south, there’s a sense that the institute is running out of friends and time.
While the median founder, investor, or civil servant will cheerfully roll their eyes at the mention of the ATI, what’s less understood is
why
the UK’s national AI institute has proven such a flop, despite spending over quarter of a billion pounds since its inception. To piece this together, I’ve spoken to current and former Turing insiders, figures from the world of research funding, academics, and civil servants.
Subscribe
Set up to fail?
To understand the ATI, we need to understand the circumstances of its creation. Back in 2014, we had hit the peak of the ‘big data’ hype cycle.
Gartner Emerging Technologies Hype Cycle - 2013
As data storage costs tumbled, big tech companies printed money, and the cloud became the rage - the UK Government decided it wanted a piece of the action. ‘Big data’ had been identified as one of the UK’s ‘Eight Great Technologies in 2013’, unlocking new funds for consultancies
to produce pdfs
on public sector innovation.
In the 2014 Budget, George Osborne
announced
that the UK would invest £42 million over five years into a data science institute, dedicated to the memory of Alan Turing. From day one, the goals of the institute were nebulous. The official government announcement stated that the institute would
“collaborate and work closely with other e-infrastructure and big-data investments across the UK Research Base”
, as well
“attracting the best talent and investment from across the globe”
.
The task of bringing this ambition to life fell to the Engineering & Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), a powerful public body tasked with allocating money to research and postgraduate degrees. In July, a few months after the Budget announcement, the EPSRC
called for expressions of interest
from university partners. It would go on to announce Cambridge, Edinburgh, Oxford, UCL and Warwick as its initial partners following a competition to which over 20 universities applied. It has since expanded its university partnerships to a network of over 60.
The government announced that
the ATI would
have a headquarters in the British Library in London (after turning down
a bid from Liverpool
), along with “spurs” in businesses and universities. This would
“bring benefits to the whole country … including in our great northern cities”
, despite no academic institutions from the latter making the cut.
Creating a national data science institute in partnership with some of the UK’s top universities might seem like a logical move. But arguably, this was the root from which all of the ATI’s ills stemmed.
A virtual institute
By outsourcing the institute to the universities, the EPSRC guaranteed th
43493313.article_summary: 《如何不建立一个AI研究所：艾伦·图灵研究所的失败》一文揭示了英国国家AI研究所面临的危机。尽管2024年获得了1亿英镑的新 funding，艾伦·图灵研究所（ATI）仍计划大规模裁员并削减四分之一的研究项目，员工公开反抗。尽管2023年生成式AI热潮席卷全球，ATI却未能引领潮流，反而处于防御状态。批评指出，ATI未能在AI关键进展如大型语言模型（LLM）和通用人工智能（AGI）上发挥预期作用。英国研究与创新机构对ATI的审查也对其治理和财务管理提出批评。文章分析了ATI失败的原因，包括创建时目标模糊、过度依赖大学合作以及未能适应AI快速发展。尽管投入超过2.5亿英镑，ATI仍未能实现其预期目的。

data.title: First-of-its-kind trial enables paralysed man to stand via stem cell injection
data.author: bentobean
data.article_summary: 日本一项开创性试验中，四位瘫痪患者接受了源自诱导多能干细胞（iPS细胞）的神经干细胞注射治疗。其中一名日本男子能够自行站立，另一名患者可以移动手臂和腿，但其余两人未见显著改善。试验由东京庆应大学的科学家Hideyuki Okano及其团队进行，结果显示治疗是安全的，但尚需更大规模试验验证疗效。iPS细胞被转化为神经前体细胞，注射到患者脊髓损伤部位，希望其能分化为神经元和胶质细胞。所有患者在术后一年内未见严重副作用。尽管部分患者有显著恢复，但也有可能为自然康复。全球每年约90万人遭遇脊髓损伤，研究为治疗此类损伤带来新希望。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： stem细胞治疗脊髓损伤的有效性、安全性、免疫排斥问题以及实际应用情况。

不同观点：
• [lambdaone] 认为文章表明治疗可能帮助患者站立，但其他患者的治疗没有明显效果，且有效案例中不能排除自然恢复的可能性。不过该治疗显示出一定的安全性，未来值得进一步研究。
• [bufferoverflow] 提供了一篇2015年的学术文章，讨论了人类胚胎干细胞治疗脊髓损伤的研究，暗示该领域已有一定研究基础。
• [narrator] 提到一个十年前在Reddit上分享自己干细胞治疗经历的案例，该患者在接受中国注射治疗后重新行走，但遭到其他用户质疑。这表明干细胞治疗在实际应用中存在信息不对称和信任问题。
• [kylehotchkiss] 质疑使用他人DNA的干细胞如何避免免疫系统的排斥反应，认为使用自体干细胞更合理，类似于自体骨髓移植。

争议焦点：
• 干细胞治疗的真实有效性和免疫排斥问题。

Nerve cells derived from induced pluripotent stem cells have the potential to reverse paralysis.
Credit: IKELOS GmbH/Dr. Christopher B. Jackson/SPL
A paralysed man can stand on his own after receiving an injection of neural stem cells to treat his spinal cord injury. The Japanese man was one of four individuals in a
first-of-its-kind trial
that used reprogrammed stem cells to treat people who are paralysed.
Another man can now move his arms and legs following the treatment, but the two others did not show substantial improvements. The trial was run by Hideyuki Okano, a stem-cell scientist at Keio University in Tokyo, and his colleagues.
The results, which were announced at a press conference on 21 March and have not yet been peer reviewed, suggest that the treatment is safe, say researchers.
“That’s a great positive outcome. It’s very exciting for the field,” says James St John, a translational neuroscientist at Griffith University in the Gold Coast, Australia.
Previous trials using other types of stem cell have also demonstrated that the therapy is safe, but have so far shown mixed results. “Nothing’s really worked so far,” says St John.
Larger trials will be needed to establish whether the improvements observed in the two individuals in the current study were a result of the treatment. It’s possible the patients experienced a natural recovery, says St John.
In 2019, roughly 0.9 million people globally experienced a spinal cord injury, and some 20 million people were living with the condition
1
.
Reprogrammed cells
Reprogrammed or induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells are created by reverting adult cells to an embryonic-like state, from which they can be coaxed to develop into other cell types.
In this trial, iPS cells derived from a donor were used to create neural precursor cells. Two million of these were injected into each patient’s injury site, in the hope that they would eventually develop into neurons and glial cells.
The trial’s first surgery was performed in December 2021; the other three were conducted between 2022 and 2023. All four recipients were adult males and two were aged 60 or older. They all had surgery between two and four weeks after the damage was done, says Okano. Recipients were given immune-suppressing drugs to prevent their bodies from attacking the cells for six months after the surgery.
The results are the latest in a series of small human trials testing the potential of iPS cells to
regenerate tissue
and
treat disease
.
Learning to walk
At the one-year follow-up, the researchers did not observe any serious adverse effects.
All individuals started the trial with the highest injury classification of A, as measured by the American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS). People with this level of impairment have no sensory or motor function below the point of injury. Two of the participants did not show improvements in their ability to feel or move in the lowest section of their spinal cord. One individual moved up to a classification of C in the period after surgery, and can move some of their arm and leg muscles but cannot stand on their own. Another individual improved to a level D (normal function is classified as E) and can stand independently. “That person is now training to walk,” says Okano. “This is a dramatic recovery.”
Preliminary analysis of the data suggests the treatment works, says Okano.

43463779.article_summary: 日本一项开创性试验中，四位瘫痪患者接受了源自诱导多能干细胞（iPS细胞）的神经干细胞注射治疗。其中一名日本男子能够自行站立，另一名患者可以移动手臂和腿，但其余两人未见显著改善。试验由东京庆应大学的科学家Hideyuki Okano及其团队进行，结果显示治疗是安全的，但尚需更大规模试验验证疗效。iPS细胞被转化为神经前体细胞，注射到患者脊髓损伤部位，希望其能分化为神经元和胶质细胞。所有患者在术后一年内未见严重副作用。尽管部分患者有显著恢复，但也有可能为自然康复。全球每年约90万人遭遇脊髓损伤，研究为治疗此类损伤带来新希望。
43463779.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [bentobean] 提供了一个存档链接，可能与讨论相关，但没有详细说明内容。
• [sharpshadow] 表达了对干细胞治疗未来潜力的乐观看法，并希望用于治疗脑损伤，显示出对该技术更广泛应用的期待。

data.title: Philosophy of Coroutines (2023)
data.author: HeliumHydride
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了协程的哲学及其应用，作者Simon Tatham自20世纪90年代中期以来一直对协程充满热情。协程的客观优势在于其相较于显式状态机和传统线程的实用性。主观上，作者喜欢协程是因为它们符合其对代码清晰度的追求。文章探讨了如何充分利用协程的技巧，包括何时使用协程及其适用类型，如生成器、消费者、适配器和协议等。协程可大可小，结合输入队列和预过滤器能发挥更大作用。作者还介绍了不同协程范式，如TAOCP中的对称、无栈协程。尽管作者在C语言中通过预处理器技巧模拟协程，但他也乐见协程在更多编程语言中得到支持，特别是C++20中的协程系统。文章总结了协程的广泛用途及其在代码编写中的独特优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕协程（coroutines）的优点、实现方式、语法问题及实际应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• **协程的优势与实现**：
  - **prngl**：对协程持积极态度，认为协程在状态机和并发编程中是非常好的抽象工具。他提到可以通过分配协程栈并使用'yield'函数切换栈指针来实现协程，这种方式甚至可以用于没有内建协程支持的语言如C，并提供了相关的库链接（minicoro和zigcoro）。他还推荐了一篇关于Lua协程的文章。
  - **tkcranny**：分享了自己在实际项目中使用协程的成功经验，尤其是在处理API请求、监听socket、处理数据冲突等方面，认为协程让代码更加自然和优雅，特别是在复杂的UI应用中，协程的纯状态聚焦特性使得逻辑测试和推理变得更加容易。

• **协程语法与"await"、"async"的争议**：
  - **ktpsns**：对协程语法中的"await"和"async"关键字在Python和Rust中的广泛使用表示不满，认为这些关键字造成了样板代码（boilerplate）。他提到了“函数颜色问题”（what color is your function），质疑是否存在更简洁的解决方案。

• **协程在实际开发中的替代方案**：
  - **VikingCoder**：不喜欢手写状态机，分享了自己在开发基于文本的冒险游戏时，通过使用独立的线程和AutoResetEvents来管理逻辑和UI，避免了使用async/await，简化了代码，并使得测试更加容易。

补充讨论：
• **协程库与工具**：
  - **prngl**：提到了C语言中的minicoro库和Zig语言中的zigcoro库，并分享了一篇关于Lua协程的文章，为希望了解协程实现的人提供了资源。

• **协程相关的小工具和语法补充**：
  - **robertlagrant**：提到Python中的itertools.pairwise函数，认为这种简单但未包含在标准库中的工具在实际开发中非常实用。

争议焦点：
• 协程语法中的"await"和"async"关键字在实际使用中是否造成了不必要的复杂性和样板代码，以及是否存在更简洁的语法设计。

总结：评论中对协程的整体功能和优势持积极态度，但在具体语法和实际应用上存在分歧，尤其是对"async/await"关键字的争议以及协程在不同场景下的实现方式和替代方案。

Coroutines large and small

Conclusion

Introduction
Iâve been a huge fan of coroutines since the mid-1990s.
I encountered the idea as a student, when I first read
The
Art of Computer Programming
. Iâd been programming already
for most of my childhood, and I was completely blown away by the
idea, which was entirely new to me. In fact, itâs probably not
an exaggeration to say that in the whole of
TAOCP
that
was the single thing that changed my life the most.
Within a few months of encountering the idea for the first
time, I found myself wanting to use it in real code, during a
vacation job at a (now defunct) tech company. Sadly I was coding
in C at the time, which didnât support coroutines. But I didnât
let that stop me: I came up with a C preprocessor trick that
worked well enough to fake them, and did it anyway.
The trick I came up with has limitations, but itâs reliable
enough to use in serious code. I wrote it up a few years later
in the
article â
Coroutines
in C
â, and Iâve been using it ever since, in both C and C++,
whenever the code Iâm trying to write looks as if it would be
most naturally expressed in that style.
Or rather, I do that in code bases
where I can get away
with it
, because itâs unquestionably a weird and unorthodox
style of C by normal standards, and not everyone is prepared to
take it in their stride. Mostly I limit my use of C-preprocessor
coroutines to free software projects where Iâm the lead or only
developer (in
particular,
PuTTY
and
spigot
),
because there, I get to choose whatâs an acceptable coding style
and whatâs not. The only time Iâve ever used the same technique
in code I wrote for an employer was in that original vacation
job where I invented the trick â and Iâm sure I only got away
with it that time because my team didnât practise code
review.
Of course, Iâm also happy to use coroutine-style idioms in any
language where you
donât
have to resort to trickery,
such as using generators in Python whenever it seems like a good
idea.
Whenever I
canât
use coroutines, I feel limited,
because itâs become second nature to me to spot parts of a
program that
want
to be written in coroutine style, and
would be more awkward to express in other ways. So Iâm very much
in favour of coroutines becoming more mainstream â and Iâve been
pleased to see support appearing in more and more languages over
the decades. At the time of writing this, Wikipedia has
an
impressive
list of languages
that now include coroutine support; from
my own perspective, the big ones are Python generators, and the
addition of a coroutine system to C++20.
I recently got round
to
learning
about the C++20 system
in detail. In the course of that, I
had conversations about coroutines with several friends and
colleagues, which made me think more seriously about the fact
that Iâm so fond of them, and wonder if I had anything more
specific to say about that than âtheyâre really usefulâ.
It turned out that I did. So this article presents my
âphilosophy of coroutinesâ:
why
I find them so useful,
what kinds of thing theyâre useful for, tricks Iâve learned for
getting the most out of them, and even a few different ways of
thinking
about
them.
But it discusses coroutines as a general concept, not specific
to their implementation in any particular language. So where I
present code snippets, theyâll be in whatever language is
convenient to the example, or even in pure pseudocode.
Why Iâm so enthusiastic about coroutines
Go on then, why
do
I like coroutines so much?
Well, from first principles, there are two possibilities.
Either itâs because they really are awesome, or itâs because
they suit my personal taste. (Or a combination of the two, of
course.)
I can think of arguments for both of those positions, but I
donât think I have the self-awareness to decide which is mor

data.title: Dagger: A shell for the container age
data.author: gk1
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了Dagger Shell，这是一款基于Bash语法的前端工具，用于Dagger Engine运行和组合系统。Dagger Shell旨在补充传统系统壳层（system shell），通过简单模块和标准接口来替代复杂的工作流，而非依赖脆弱的单体结构。它支持容器、秘密信息、服务端点等原生功能，所有操作默认在沙盒中运行，确保可重复性和快速迭代。

Dagger Shell不仅允许用户通过终端执行构建、测试、部署等任务，还可以与多种编程语言的SDK结合，将壳层与API结合，提供跨语言的模块生态。文章还展示了如何利用Dagger Shell创建Alpine容器、设置开发环境和进行多阶段测试等操作，强调壳层和代码是实现软件自动化的两大核心要素。Dagger Shell旨在简化现代软件堆栈的复杂性，让用户专注于壳层和代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dagger 工具的定位和用途，及其与现有工具（如 Jenkins、Docker）的关系和竞争。

不同观点：
• [randomtechguy] 认为 Dagger 最初旨在替代 Jenkins，提供在本地运行和调试 CI 管道的功能，但现在开发方向变得分散，试图替代 Docker、成为新的 shell，甚至涉及 langchain。他认为功能复杂化并不意味着更好，新的一套复杂 CLI 参数并没有解决根本问题。
• [a_t48] 对 Dagger 持积极态度，认为它可以解决 Dockerfile 和 shell 脚本混合使用时的混乱问题，尤其是在不同环境（开发机、CI 等）下运行不同挂载和参数时。
• [ledauphin] 对 Dagger 试图替代 Docker 的宏大愿景表示赞赏，但对其使用 bash 兼容性持保留态度，认为应该寻找超越 bash 的工具。
• [jatins] 认为 Dagger 的描述过于泛泛，认为其“组合引擎”的定位没有独特性，并指出很多工具都可以称为组合引擎。
• [cedws] 对 Dagger 的管道设计表示困惑，认为与 bash 管道的直观性相比，Dagger 的管道设计缺乏明确的流动和过程。

补充讨论：
• [shykes] 提到有人为 Dagger Shell 脚本创建了 web UI，提供笔记本格式编排工具。
• [throwdaggeraway] 对 Dagger 持负面态度，认为其在底层细节上耗费太多时间，不如 Nix 和 Bazel 等工具提供清晰的边界和可预测的结果。
• [jbverschoor] 自我推广其 Docker shell 容器项目，将讨论引向相关工具。
• [mrbluecoat] 提到 Dagger 类似于在容器内进行开发的工具，并引用了 Jetify 和 Flix 作为对比。
• [hamandcheese] 作为 Nix 重度用户，认为 Dagger 介于 Dockerfile 和实际代码定义软件之间，吸引力不大。
• [xedeon] 提到 Dagger 让他想起其他工具如 Envy 和一个相关视频，将讨论扩展到类似工具。
• [remram] 对 Dagger 的实际用途表示困惑，要求明确其替代的程序和活动。
• [tonymet] 建议 Dagger 提供在 Dockerfile 某一步进入容器调试的功能，认为这样可以避免学习新语法。
• [elorm] 质疑 Dagger 是否改变了产品定位，从独立的 pipeline-as-code 服务转向试图重建 Docker。
• [Kinrany] 对管道作为方法调用的设计表示困惑，质疑其是否真正实现了程序组合。

争议焦点：
• Dagger 的定位是否清晰及其与现有工具（如 Jenkins、Docker）的关系。
• Dagger 的功能复杂化是否真正解决了问题，还是增加了不必要的复杂性。
• Dagger 管道设计与传统 bash 管道直观性的对比。

The Unix shell is over 50 years old, but it still defines how programmers use their computers. We type a few words in a terminal, and milliseconds later an ephemeral factory comes online: the Unix pipeline. Data streams through a network of simple programs working concurrently, like robots on the factory floor, executing a computational choreography we composed seconds ago. Its job done, the factory vanishes. Onto the next command. That loop built the internet, and still runs it today.
The design principles of Unix are timeless: write simple programs, compose them with standard interfaces. But 50 years is a long timeâ¦ the software stack has expanded, and Unix interfaces are buried under layers of abstraction. We still use the shell, but itâs no longer the universal composition system it was meant to be. What if we changed that?
What if the Unix shell took the best ideas from docker, make, powershell and nix? Native support for primitives like containers, secrets and service endpoints; typed objects; declarative execution; content-addressed artifacts; everything sandboxed and cached by default. What if those all became standard shell features, available with standard shell syntax, and backed by a modern API? Would we still need to learn a dozen DSLs to automate the basic tasks of shipping software? Or would the complexity of the modern software stack melt away, leaving only two fundamental elements: shell and code? Letâs find out!
Today weâre introducing Dagger Shell: a bash syntax frontend for our state-of-the-art runtime and composition system, the Dagger Engine. Use it for builds, tests, ephemeral environments, deployments, or any other task you want to automate from the terminal. Itâs also a great way to
compose AI agents
â¦but more on that later.
To get started, just
install the latest version of Dagger
, and type
dagger
. Or keep reading for examples.
A complement to your system shell
Dagger Shell isnât meant to replace your system shell, but to complement it. When a workflow is too complex to fit in a regular shell, the next available option is often a brittle monolith: not as simple as a shell script, not as robust as full-blown software. The Dagger Shell aspires to help you replace that monolith with a collection of simple modules, composed with standard interfaces.
container |
from alpine |
with-exec apk add
git
Shell and code are all you need
When a script becomes too complex and outgrows the shell syntax, why learn a weird DSL when you can write real code?
Unix was built on the twin pillars of its shell and C programming environment. Dagger follows the same model, with SDKs available for Go, Python, Typescript, Java and PHP. Pick a language, write a functionâ¦Congratulations, you just extended Dagger with your own primitive! No matter how complex your system, you should only ever need two building blocks: shell and code.
Shell, meet API
Dagger Shell is just another Dagger API client, giving you typed objects, built-in documentation, and access to a
cross-language ecosystem of reusable modules
.
Thatâs right, Dagger Shell can load any of the thousands of modules in the Daggerverse, inspect their API, and run their functions. Here we explore a
Trivy module
:
Sandboxed by default
Dagger Shell commands run as sandboxed functions, accessing host resources (files, secrets, services) only when explicitly provided as arguments.
This can make commands slightly more verbose, but also more repeatable, giving you confidence to iterate quickly without second-guessing.
For example, hereâs a dev environment using a secret, local directory, and database access:
Simple container build
This creates an Alpine container, drops in a text file with your message, sets it to display that message when run, and publishes it to a temporary registry. All in one pipeline - no context switching between Dockerfile creation, build commands, and registry pushes.
Test environments
A common problem in CI is creating ephemeral test environments: you need to containerize the software being tested, and connect it to its dependencies. Dagger makes this easy with native support for service bindings.
For example, letâs create an environment with several live instances of the Dagger docs hooked up, and âtestâ them with curl.
This also highlights how third-party modules can be seamlessly mixed and matched.
# Build a wolfi linux container with curl, then test connection to stable and dev docs
github.com/dagger/dagger/modules/wolfi | container
--packages
=
curl
|
with-service-binding docs-stable
$(github.com/dagger/dagger/docs@v0.17.1 | server)
|
with-service-binding docs-dev
$(github.com/dagger/dagger/docs@main | server)
|
with-exec
curl
http://docs-stable |
with-exec
curl

data.title: Banned Books: Analysis of Censorship on Amazon.com (2024)
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary:
本文分析了亚马逊在美国"amazon.com"平台上限制某些产品运往特定地区的情况。研究发现，亚马逊限制了17,050种产品向至少一个地区的 shipping，其中书籍是最常被限制的类别。被禁书籍主要涉及LGBTIQ、宗教神秘学、色情、基督教以及健康与保健等主题。受影响地区包括阿联酋、沙特阿拉伯等中东国家以及文莱、巴布亚新几内亚、塞舌尔和赞比亚。

亚马逊使用误导性错误信息（如产品暂时缺货）来解释限制原因，这违反了其对LGBTIQ权利的公开承诺。研究还发现了一些过度或错误分类的限制案例，例如与乳腺癌相关的书籍和"Gay Science"等作品。

报告最后向亚马逊提出了多项建议，以解决其 censorship 问题并改善用户体验。

• [sleiben] 提到两年前在德国亚马逊上无法购买Oriana Fallaci的《The Rage and the Pride》，感觉像是审查。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于亚马逊审查和禁售书籍的范围和动机，特别是涉及LGBTQ材料和仇恨言论的问题。
• 不同用户对亚马逊商业行为的道德性和合法性有不同的看法，有些人认为这是企业正常的盈利行为，有些人则认为这是对人权和言论自由的侵犯。
• 讨论中还提到了被禁书籍的定义和实际影响，包括哪些书籍在不同国家和平台上被禁以及其背后的原因。

43497264.article_content:
Key findings
We analyze the system Amazon deploys on the US “amazon.com” storefront to restrict shipments of certain products to specific regions. We found 17,050 products that Amazon restricted from being shipped to at least one world region.
While many of the shipping restrictions are related to regulations involving WiFi, car seats, and other heavily regulated product categories, the most common product category restricted by Amazon in our study was books.
Banned books were largely related to LGBTIQ, the occult, erotica, Christianity, and health and wellness. The regions affected by this censorship were the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and many other Middle Eastern countries as well as Brunei Darussalam, Papua New Guinea, Seychelles, and Zambia. In our test sample, Amazon censored over 1.1% of the books sold on amazon.com in at least one of these regions.
We identified three major censorship blocklists which Amazon assigns to different regions. In numerous cases, the resulting censorship is either overly broad or miscategorized. Examples include the restriction of books relating to breast cancer, recipe books invoking “food porn” euphemisms, Nietzsche’s
Gay Science
, and “rainbow” Mentos candy.
To justify why restricted products cannot be shipped, Amazon uses varying error messages such as by conveying that an item is temporarily out of stock. In misleading its customers and censoring books, Amazon is violating its public commitments to both LGBTIQ and more broadly human rights.
We conclude our report by providing Amazon multiple
recommendations
to address concerns raised by our work.
Introduction
The rise in online shopping has led to more global reach into markets that may otherwise be inaccessible for companies through traditional retail channels. This increased reach brings new opportunities but also has its own challenges for global e-commerce retailers. One such challenge is in dealing with different, more restrictive regulatory environments worldwide.
In this report, we analyze American e-commerce retailer Amazon and its system for preventing shipments of certain products to certain world regions as it is implemented on the US storefront — amazon.com. Specifically, we analyze functionality that Amazon implements to
restrict
shipments of certain products to certain regions even if the product is available and sellers are offering to ship it there. While Amazon normally hides this restriction system from customers using misleading error messages, we employ a novel methodology to uncover and measure on which products and in which regions it is activated by peeling back the layers of Amazon’s website and analyzing its internal workings. Notably, our method can distinguish between a product being restricted by Amazon and it being organically unavailable in a region.
In total, we found 17,050 products that were restricted from being shipped to at least one world region. While many of the shipping restrictions observed in our study are related to regulations involving WiFi, car seats, and other heavily regulated product categories, the most common product category restricted by Amazon was books. Banned books were largely related to LGBTIQ, the occult, erotica, Christianity, and health and wellness. More broadly, books were the victims of
censorship
, which in this report we define as Amazon’s restriction of product shipment under political or religious motivation. The regions commonly affected by this censorship were the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Saudi Arabia, and many other Middle Eastern countries as well as Brunei Darussalam, Papua New Guinea, Seychelles, and Zambia.
Given that the topics censored include LGBTIQ, our findings call into question Amazon’s
public commitment to LGBTIQ rights
as well as its respect for the rights of its users at large. By censoring the availability of books, Amazon is depriving its users of valuable information. Furthermore, by communicating to customers that censored products are organically unavailable (e.g., being out of stock), Amazon is depriving customers of the ability to make informed decisions. We conclude our report by making multiple recommendations to Amazon.
Background
In this section we briefly describe Amazon’s history as it relates to our analysis. We then outline some of the regulations applying to Amazon’s business in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and China, which are some of the more restrictive regulatory environments to which products on amazon.com can be shipped.
Amazon background
Amazon is an American multinational company that originated as an online bookseller and has since evolved into a global e-commerce marketplace. Amazon’s business is heavily focused on managing
shipping logistics internationally and serving a global consumer base
. Alongside the main e-commerce platform, they also provide cloud computing services (Amazon Web Services), consumer electronics (Amazon Kindle and Amazon Echo), and online streaming (Amazon Prime Video) among other offerings.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高能效窗技术的进步、成本、应用及实际效果

不同观点：
• [eagerpace] 认为高能效窗技术虽好，但成本较高，尤其是与普通窗相比，能源高效窗的价格通常高出50%，使得大多数房主将其视为奢侈品。长期回报不如其他家居升级明显，需要激励措施来促进普及。
• [notmyspacetom] 介绍了LuxWall公司生产的真空隔热窗，像保温瓶一样工作，能大幅减少热传导和热对流，适合旧建筑改造，能有效降低能耗。
• [mrbigbob] 提到了MIT的衍生公司Aeroshield，开发了透明气凝胶材料，预计2026年上市，可能较昂贵，但具有很高的能效潜力。
• [FuriouslyAdrift] 分享了使用防弹玻璃的经验，厚达6英寸，虽然主要用于隔音，但暗示了多层玻璃在隔热和隔音方面的优势。
• [jml7c5] 认为文章中提到的三层和四层玻璃窗并不是新概念，只是采用了超薄内层玻璃，降低了成本和重量，而非全新的技术突破。
• [mock-possum] 作为房主，表达了对高能效窗的渴望，但认为这是奢侈品，难以负担，尤其是在已有房屋中更换窗户。
• [jeppine] 建议拥有1940年代前历史房屋的房主保留原窗并进行修复，认为除非使用四层或六层窗，否则节能效果有限，且原窗美观耐用。
• [tristor] 分享了个人经验，指出更换窗户虽然提升了居住质量，但并未增加房屋转售时的市场价格，且成本高昂。认为除非定制房屋，否则难以获得高质量窗户。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于高能效窗技术的实际应用成本与效果。虽然技术上有显著进步，但高成本与市场接受度成为推广的主要障碍。
• 一些评论提到了特定产品和公司的例子，如LuxWall和Aeroshield，展示了技术发展的前沿。
• 历史窗的保护与修复也被提及，强调了在节能与历史保护之间找到平衡的重要性。
• 总体上，讨论反映了对高质量窗户的需求与现实中成本和市场接受度的矛盾。

data.author: Anon84

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学习理论（learning theory）书籍的价值和作用，及其与实际应用的关系。

不同观点：
• [commandersaki] 对学习理论从基本原理开始的价值抱有期待，暗示这种讨论可能较少。他认为理论学习有重要意义，但没有深入展开。

• [esafak] 分享了相关学习理论的书籍链接，提供了进一步的资源，但没有明确表达对理论学习的态度或观点。

• [miltava] 对不同学习理论书籍（如《Foundations of Machine Learning》）在深度和易理解性方面进行比较，表现出对书籍实用性的关注，并希望了解新书籍在这方面的表现。

• [grg0] 对分享的资源表示感谢，支持此类学习资源的传播，但没有深入讨论理论学习的价值问题。

• [almostgotcaught] 强烈质疑学习理论书籍的实用性，认为许多传统理论（如SVM、贝叶斯网络、核方法等）在现代大规模机器学习应用中已不再重要。他主张教学应更注重实用技能，而非复杂的数学理论。他还指出，深度学习的成功更多依赖于数据量和计算力，而非理论的精妙。

补充讨论：
• [almostgotcaught] 的观点引发了关于理论与实践之间关系的争议。他认为现代机器学习实践更多依赖于经验和数据，而非理论分析，因此质疑学习理论的价值。这一观点与其他用户分享学习资源、探讨理论深度的行为形成对比，显示出理论与实践在机器学习领域中的潜在张力。

• 争议的焦点在于学习理论（如浓度不等式、PAC学习等）在现代机器学习实践中的实际价值。一方认为这些理论是基础，对深入理解机器学习有帮助；另一方则认为这些理论在实际应用中已经过时，教学应更注重实用技能。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是比较不同学习理论书籍的深度和易理解性，反映出读者在选择学习资源时的实际需求和关注点。

data.title: Emacs Solo: A Surprise System Crafters Live Demo
data.author: JNRowe
data.article_summary: Rahul M. Juliato在其博客中分享了Emacs Solo配置在System Crafters Weekly Show上进行的 live demo 所带来的惊喜。Emacs Solo是一个极简配置，旨在利用Emacs内置功能实现高效工作流，不依赖外部包。该配置强调轻量、快速和功能性，包括增强的icomplete-vertical功能、git-gutter-like特性、eshell定制、多项搜索编辑、内置新闻阅读器、高级文件对比和版本控制、扩展的viper模式、Tree-sitter模式、LSP配置以及自定义的rainbow-mode等。Rahul感谢David Wilson和System Crafters社区的支持，并表达了对社区贡献者的感激。这次demo让他深受启发，并鼓励大家探索Emacs Solo的GitHub仓库以了解更多。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs及其相关工具的使用和社区参与

不同观点：
• [rahen] 认为Eshell是一个被低估的shell，并提到自己越来越少依赖tmux和脚本，而更多地使用Elisp宏和基于Emacs的应用。他强调Emacs的可高度定制性，并将其视为自由软件精神的体现，建议那些仅将Emacs视为编辑器或VS Code前身的人阅读一些相关文章。
• [bigeatie] 推荐System Crafters社区，邀请感兴趣的人加入IRC频道或论坛，以促进社区互动和资源共享。
• [baruchthescribe] 提到David Williams的Emacs Solo演示 inspiring，并表示自己曾尝试在一两个月内专注使用Emacs以测试其生产力。他还提到曾考虑使用带有Emacs键绑定的VS Code作为另一种选择。

补充讨论：
• [rahen] 提供了两个链接，以支持其观点，强调Emacs作为可高度定制和开放的TUI框架，并呼吁用户深入探索Emacs的功能和潜力。
• [bigeatie] 侧重于社区参与，提供了具体的联系方式和资源，以帮助他人加入和利用社区支持。
• [baruchthescribe] 分享了个人体验，对Emacs和VS Code的结合使用表现出兴趣，反映了不同工具之间功能互补的可能性。

争议焦点：
• 对Emacs的定位存在不同看法。一部分人（如rahen）强调Emacs的深度定制和自由软件精神，而另一部分人（如baruchthescribe）则关注Emacs与其他工具（如VS Code）的结合使用。这反映了用户在工具选择和使用方式上的多样性和偏好差异。

Rahul's Blog

Emacs Solo: A Surprise System Crafters Live Demo
Rahul M. Juliato
Rahul M. Juliato
March	27, 2025
#
emacs
#
systemcrafters

demo
Last Friday, I was genuinely surprised by a live demo of my
Emacs
Solo
configuration on the
System Crafters Weekly Show
. Watching
the live demo was an eye-opener, as I hadn't expected the project to
get such attention, especially in a live setting. Seeing
David
Wilson
take a deep dive into the setup, testing the configuration
live, and exploring how powerful Emacs can be with only its built-in
packages was both humbling and inspiring.
For more details and to explore the configuration yourself, visit the
Emacs Solo GitHub
repository
.
The
Emacs Solo
configuration is all about returning to the roots
of Emacs. It's a minimalist setup designed to challenge myself and
test the full potential of Emacs using only its built-in
functionality. The goal was to create an efficient, yet fully
functional environment, all while keeping things as light and fast as
possible. No external dependencies, no clutter. Just pure,
unadulterated Emacs.
The Project: Emacs Solo
Emacs Solo
is a configuration that embraces the power of Emacs
without relying on external packages. It's a setup I go back to from
time to time to remind myself of how much can be accomplished with
just what Emacs offers out of the box.
This configuration is designed to be both powerful and lightweight,
allowing for a fast, efficient workflow with a focus on simplicity and
minimalism. The project includes several useful features for
day-to-day tasks like searching, editing, and navigating—everything
you need for an efficient Emacs experience.
Some of the highlights of the project include:
» A preview of
icomplete-verical
enhancements I proposed to the
Emacs core team (custom prefixes, vertico style setup, and inline
completion closer to corfu/company that works on text buffers and
eshell).
» An experimental custom
git-gutter-like
feature.
» Supercharged eshell customization.
» Custom solutions for editing multiple search entries.
» Built-in news readers like Gnus and Newsticker.
» Advanced file diffing and version control.
» Extended viper mode for those who prefer vim-style editing.
» Tree-sitter modes.
» LSP configurations.
» Custom
rainbown-mode
like.
» And many customizations of built-in packages.
The idea is that Emacs is already a powerful IDE, and with a bit of
clever customization, it can be made into something even more
streamlined, adaptable, and effective without the need for external
packages.
Watch the Demo
Here's the video of the live demo from the
System Crafters Weekly
Show
:
» Also available here
Conclusion
I’d like to take this opportunity to thank
David Wilson
for the
amazing show and to the
System Crafters
community for their
continued support and enthusiasm around Emacs. I also want to express
my gratitude to everyone who has contributed code that I’ve borrowed
and learned from over the years. Particularly
Gopar
and
Protesilaos
. Without the shared knowledge and experience from
these fantastic people, the
Emacs Solo
project wouldn't have been
possible.
As always, the beauty of Emacs lies in its community, and I'm grateful
for all the inspiration, contributions, and shared wisdom that make
projects like
Emacs Solo
come to life. Thank you to everyone who
continues to inspire and teach me along the way.

data.title: Most promoted and blocked domains on Kagi
data.author: lucgommans
data.article_summary: Kagi是一个致力于提供更人性化网络搜索体验的平台，拥有43,403名会员、4,547个家庭和126个团队使用其服务。平台在过去一天处理了845,200次查询和11,969次助手线程。Kagi允许用户自定义域名 popularity，并列出被推广和阻止最多的域名，如pinterest.com、foxnews.com等。Kagi提供多种键盘快捷键和搜索操作符，支持DuckDuckGo的"bang"命令，并提供计算、翻译、定时器等多种小工具。Kagi还提供多种计划和隐私条款，致力于提升搜索体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kagi搜索引擎的使用情况、网站排名和用户反馈

不同观点：
• [fumufumufumu] 认为Kagi的使用者主要是网络开发者，并质疑Kagi是否能吸引更多非网络开发者用户，担心其未来发展。他指出，排名前列的网站大多与软件开发相关，尤其是网络开发。

• [neilv] 赞赏Arch Linux wiki的高排名，尽管自己使用Debian系统，但认为Arch Linux wiki能够解答许多与Debian相关的问题，特别是关于Xmonad的非发行版特定问题。

• [titaphraz] 对Pinterest占据前七名 blocked results表示认可，并批评Google让Pinterest破坏了Google Image搜索结果。

• [Brajeshwar] 提到Kagi对登录用户和公共用户展示不同结果，并分享自己穿Kagi T恤却未被认出的经历，表达对Kagi品牌认知度的失望。

• [0xTJ] 对w3schools.com的高排名不感惊讶，但认为其内容对实际编码帮助不大，基于自身经验认为该网站的文档价值有限。

• [rcyeh] 提到自己的Kagi列表与总体排名高度相关，质疑Kagi是否为用户优化了有用的文档网站，如docs.python.org和cppreference.com。

• [bcoates] 指出alternativeto.net和纽约时报在Kagi上既被提升又被禁止的现象，认为这是最具分歧的排名结果。

• [Sxubas] 质疑healthline在block/lower列表中的高排名，认为其提供可信的健康信息，并链接来源，具有一定可信度。

• [claytonjy] 对Kagi的每日查询量低于百万感到惊讶，质疑这是Kagi整体查询量还是仅为部分子集。

• [knowknow] 对TikTok在block列表中排名第三表示疑惑，质疑TikTok在Kagi搜索结果中出现的频率是否高于Google。

• [edelbitter] 质疑Kagi用户是否可以选择分享分析数据，或者所有用户默认同意分享这些数据。

• [kristianp] 表示很久未在Google搜索结果中看到Pinterest链接。

• [qmmmur] 想支持并付费使用Kagi，但因在澳大利亚访问速度慢而感到不便。

• [galleywest200] 对fandom.com出现在“lowered”列表中表示满意，认为尽管许多游戏已迁移到其他wiki站点，但fandom.com因SEO仍占据普通搜索结果前列。

• [CobaltFire] 对登录后自动应用block列表感到困惑，怀疑自己是否无意中使用了这些列表。

补充讨论：
Kagi的用户群体和网站排名是讨论的核心。部分用户对Kagi吸引非网络开发者能力表示怀疑，并对特定网站在搜索结果中的排名和出现频率提出质疑。此外，用户对搜索结果的个性化和数据分享政策也表示关注。访问速度和地区性问题也被提及，表明Kagi在全球范围内的可用性存在一定挑战。

43499045.article_summary: Kagi是一个致力于提供更人性化网络搜索体验的平台，拥有43,403名会员、4,547个家庭和126个团队使用其服务。平台在过去一天处理了845,200次查询和11,969次助手线程。Kagi允许用户自定义域名 popularity，并列出被推广和阻止最多的域名，如pinterest.com、foxnews.com等。Kagi提供多种键盘快捷键和搜索操作符，支持DuckDuckGo的"bang"命令，并提供计算、翻译、定时器等多种小工具。Kagi还提供多种计划和隐私条款，致力于提升搜索体验。

data.title: Asking good questions is harder than giving great answers
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 文章《提出好问题比给出好答案更难》讨论了当前用于评估AI智能的测试，指出这些测试忽略了人类探究中的一个关键方面——问题本身。作者Dan Cohen亲自尝试了为AI设计的“人类最后考试”（HLE），该考试包含3000个极具挑战性的问题，但历史问题仅占16个，且许多涉及海军战役。作者批评了这种不平衡的比例，并质疑测试是否全面评估了“人类知识”。尽管AI在回答复杂问题方面表现出色，但作者认为提出好问题更具挑战性，并强调当前的AI评估方式主要关注答案的正确性，而非问题的质量。文章还提到，尽管AI在历史研究等领域取得了显著进展，但评估方法仍有待改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于提问与回答的价值、质量以及在不同情境下的表现

不同观点：
• [magicmicah85] 提到在观看乐团演出时，观众表现的差异。一些人认为美国观众更外向，而欧洲观众则较为克制。此外，该用户提到当被知识水平较高的人认可其提问时，会感到更有成就感。
• [I_Nidhi] 质疑"Humanity’s Last Exam"是否真正衡量了人工智能的智力，认为AGI（人工通用智能）的关键在于提出有意义的新问题，而不仅仅是回答已有问题。
• [AdieuToLogic] 强调"好问题"和"好答案"都需要理解力，这是人类特有的能力，并且这些评价是由人类而非算法作出的。
• [infogulch] 观察到在论坛中，好的回答往往比好的问题更受关注。他们建议通过反过来推断：如果一个回答很好，那么其对应的问题也应该被视为好问题。
• [_DeadFred_] 分享了一种应对商务场合中提问的策略，即反问对方应该问什么问题，并计划在AI上测试这种方法。

补充讨论：
• [vismit2000] 提到一个相关的PyCon演讲，提供了有关提问价值的进一步讨论。
• [canadiantim] 指出在大语言模型时代，关于提问和回答的讨论变得更加重要。
• [charanya1234] 完全同意[vismit2000]的观点。

争议焦点：
• 提问与回答的价值评判标准，以及在不同文化背景（如美国与欧洲）中观众表现的差异。
• 人工智能是否能够提出真正有意义的新问题，从而体现其智力水平。

March 18, 2025
Asking Good Questions Is Harder Than Giving Great Answers
The tests we are using to assess the intelligence of AI are missing an essential aspect of human inquiry — the query itself
by
Dan Cohen
Jacques-Louis David, “The Death of Socrates,” 1787, Metropolitan Museum of Art. Perhaps he asked too many good questions
Recently, I sharpened a #2 pencil and took the history section of "
Humanity's Last Exam
.” Consisting of 3,000 extremely difficult questions, the test is intended for AI, not me. According to its creators and contributors, Humanity’s Last Exam will tell us when artificial general intelligence has arrived to supersede human beings, once a brilliant bot scores an A.
I got an F. Actually, worse than that: Only one of my answers was correct, and I must admit it helped that the question was multiple choice. This is fairly embarrassing for someone with a PhD in history.
What happened? Let me indulge in a standard academic humiliation-avoidance technique: examining the examiners. A much easier exercise. Of the thousands of questions on the test, a mere 16 are on history. By comparison, over 1,200 are on mathematics. This is a rather rude ratio for a purported Test of All Human Knowledge, and a major demerit in this human’s assessment of the exam.
The offense extends further to the historical topics covered. Of the 16 history questions, four of them — 25% of historical understanding! — are about naval battles. My knowledge of the displacement of various warships is admittedly weak. Other questions are byzantine, alas not literally, but figuratively, long narrative journeys with twists and turns that are clearly trying to confuse any AI by flooding its memory with countless opaque terms. Those questions certainly succeeded in confusing me.
I will not be reproducing the history questions here since the creators of Humanity’s Last Exam don’t want AI to have a sneak peek at the questions ahead of taking the test. Of course, this raises another question: Would a true superintelligence cheat? I feel like it would? If you, presumably a human reader, want to take the test yourself, you can find a database of the questions on
Hugging Face
and
GitHub
. I should also note that I did not take the “classics” section of the exam, as I am a historian of the modern era and do not know Latin, Greek, etc., but much of that section is history too, perhaps because there
were
also
naval
battles
in the ancient world.
* * *
Although I failed Humanity’s Last Exam, I did learn something about the current state of our assessment of AI, and what we expect from it. HLE’s implicit definition of “intelligence” is the ability to provide correct answers to complicated questions, and it is just one of many similar exams. Another,
less naval-gazing test
of historical knowledge is based on
a comprehensive global history database
, but still relies on question-answer pairs so it can provide numerical scores for each LLM’s ability. Upon the release of their latest models, AI companies tout improvements on these assessment tools, which allows them to proclaim definitive AI progress: “This LLM got a 92% on a PhD-level history exam, up from 56% last year!”
And the companies are not wrong about genuinely impressive improvements.
Six years ago in this newsletter
, I wrote about some initial testing I had been doing with computer vision APIs from Google and Microsoft, a first attempt to analyze the photo morgue my library had recently acquired from the
Boston Globe
. There were glimmers of hope that these pre-GPT tools could help us identify topics in millions of photographs that lacked rigorous metadata, and I found even 80% accuracy to be promising. Now our library’s digital team, much more capable than I am, has created an abstracted interface to all of the main multimodal AI services and is testing the ability of these services to provide subject headings and descriptions, with much better results (although all of the services are still imperfect).
Fellow historian Benjamin Breen
has documented similar advances
in his testing of AI. The latest models are scarily on par with a first-year doctoral student in history in some areas, able to provide solid context and advanced interpretations of documents and images, even complex ones that require substantial background in a field. The frontier models are much better than most doctoral students in other tasks, such as translation and transcription. Handwriting recognition for historical documents, in particular, has been among the hardest problems for computer scientists to solve, and cracking it will have a significant impact on historical research. Historian
Cameron Blevins has shown
that custom GPTs are now on a path to a solution that could make archives and special collections much more searchable and readable in ways that might transform our ability to do history. data.title: Take this on-call rotation and shove it
data.author: mirawelner
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了电视新闻直播中维持运作的复杂性及对技术人员的依赖。文章描述了直播涉及的各种设备和系统，如摄像机、提词器、天气预报图形等，这些设备大多可靠但偶尔会出问题。为了应对设备故障，通常需要备份系统或能解决问题的人，文章称其为“Alex”。Alex在设备出问题时负责修理，但平时有其他主要工作，如操作音频混合器。由于找到并培训这样的人才不易，Alex通常需要随时待命，甚至在家中待命以应对不同时间段的直播问题。文章指出，这种安排使得Alex的值班时间很长，尽管直播时间总共约六小时。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于自主工作和on-call（待命）工作安排的挑战与争议

不同观点：
• **boznz 的观点**：自主工作虽然回报丰厚，但on-call的压力非常大，尤其是在特定时间段内需要全天候待命，导致个人时间和休息时间被侵占。他提到在高压环境下容易犯错，并且由于独自工作，所有责任都落在他一人身上。
• **dadkins 的观点**：提倡采用轮班制，像某些SRE岗位那样明确披露夜班需求，而不是让员工在正常工作之外还要承受随时待命的压力。这种透明的安排比让员工在正常工作之外待命更合理。
• **Animats 的观点**：在加州等地区，on-call时间实际上是需要支付“待命时间”工资的。他引用了相关法律案例，指出在工会化的工作中，on-call员工通常会获得额外的报酬和最低工时保障。
• **yodsanklai 的观点**：on-call是工作中最糟糕的部分，尤其是在系统质量无法控制且没有明确所有权的情况下，问题往往被推给下一个on-call的人，导致恶性循环。
• **nhumrich 的观点**：认为on-call的问题往往是自找的，比如系统不够健壮或警报设置不合理。他主张通过改善系统来减少on-call的必要性，而不是通过支付额外报酬来解决问题。
• **purplejacket 的观点**：建议通过高额的财务激励来补偿on-call工作，例如在非工作时间以10倍正常工资支付on-call工作。这种做法可以促使公司优化on-call流程，只处理最重要的问题。
• **Artooooour 的观点**：在其所在国家，on-call的加班是有明确报酬的，员工可以选择是否接受额外工时，且公司从未在支付方面出现问题。
• **staplung 的观点**：on-call制度存在缺陷，因为它实际上鼓励员工尽量减少on-call工作的时间，而不是去解决根本问题。这导致了一种恶性循环，员工为了完成主要任务而忽视on-call职责。
• **smackeyacky 的观点**：回忆起90年代的“呼叫疯狂”经历，起初觉得on-call是一种责任的提升，但很快发现这是一种束缚。
• **mjcarden 的观点**：由于on-call的压力，他在2023年年中辞职，经过六个月才恢复到健康状态。现在的工作没有on-call的安排，待遇更好。
• **srhtftw 的观点**：on-call制度混淆了角色和责任，剥夺了开发人员的资源，最终导致倦怠。应尽快结束这种做法，以改善行业状况。

补充讨论：
• **neilv 的观点**：提到管理层在处理on-call压力时可能存在的失误，例如没有与员工沟通其困扰，并指出某些文章可能对作者有宣泄作用，但其中也包含了一些可操作的建议。同时，引用了《Soul of a New Machine》一书，反映了项目中的艰难过程。

争议焦点：
• on-call工作是否应获得额外报酬以及如何设计合理的补偿机制。
• 是否应通过改善系统和流程来减少on-call的必要性，还是通过透明的轮班制来解决on-call的压力问题。
• 员工在on-call过程中面临的责任和压力如何平衡，尤其是在系统质量无法控制的情况下。

43498213.article_content:
Take This On-Call Rotation and Shove It
Published
March 27, 2025
On This Page
The familiar blue and gold intro graphic fills the screen every evening at six o’clock on the dot. The jabbing staccato string music conjures up vague secondhand memories of what a teletype machine might have sounded like. A high angle view of the studio floor with the large Lexan-clad desk in the middle, then a cross dissolve to a two shot of the presenters for this newscast. The music fades, each person introduces themselves, then they jump straight into the top story for the evening. It’s been this way for as long as anybody can remember. They’ve never failed to get this show on the air.
They’ve never failed.
Who you gonna call?
Everything fails all the time.
Producing any sort of live television show is a complex ballet. The studio’s cameras and microphones route their signals into video switchers and audio mixers, pre-taped packages come from the video server, field reporters are connected bidirectionally through a satellite link, and with a sprinkling of pizazz from the motion graphics machine, the final product is sent off to master control and ultimately to all the kitchen counters and family rooms across the city.
But there are ancillary systems outside of this direct pipeline. The studio lighting is quite important, as most professional broadcast cameras tend to produce underwhelming images under inadequate light. The teleprompters feeding the anchors their scripts are obviously important. The weather reporting segments use an entirely separate system of graphics rendering equipment that must be linked through a chroma keyer to place the meteorologist in front of the computer-generated forecast images. And quite obviously, this equipment requires a handful of human operators.
Studio-grade equipment is obscenely expensive, but it is also incredibly reliable. It is rare for things to outright fail, but anything can eventually wear out after enough daily use. If a camera fails, perhaps they can wheel the one from the sports desk over to cover this part of the broadcast. If the teleprompters fail, the anchors have a copy of the script at their desk that they can look down at. If one of the anchors calls out sick, they can sub in talent from the morning news team.
Each of these is an example of either a redundant backup system or spare capacity that can be reallocated if needed. The broadcast technically does not need any of these contingencies to function under normal circumstances, but in cases where things go wrong it can mean the difference between success and total failure.
Not everything can be made completely redundant. A failure in the power system for the lights will most likely plunge the entire studio into darkness, and that’s no way to run a news program. Similarly, if the $50,000 video switcher dies, it’s highly unlikely that they’ll have a spare holed up in the supply closet. To insure against every possible thing that could ever go wrong, they would have to build a second studio on a separate part of the city’s electric grid, with redundant copies of all the equipment and broadcast content, along with a full crew of understudies ready to take over at a moment’s notice. This is a degree of redundancy that can’t reasonably be achieved by any budget-conscious station.
There is a hybrid between the two options, allowing the station to only maintain a single instance of anything expensive while having some assurance that the equipment they do have will work when needed: They can find an expert of some sort who is capable of fixing anything that breaks well enough to get the broadcast out. We’ll name this person Alex. If the microphone battery dies, Alex will swap it out. If the video server acts up, Alex knows how to get it working again. If the tire pressure light in the Chevrolet Weather Beast comes on, or the studio’s air conditioning fails, or the technical director breaks both their hands and needs somebody to push the buttons on their behalf, it’s Alex’s time to shine.
Now, naturally, most of the time everything is going fine and Alex has nothing to do. So Alex has some other regular job in the studio—say running the audio mixer. In fact, the audio mixer thing is their official job title and their primary responsibility at the station; they only jump into universal-problem-solving mode when something goes wrong. As soon as the problem is resolved, it’s back to the audio mixer.
The other thing about all this is, well, it’s very difficult to find and train people like Alex. So since they are at the station all evening anyway, why not also have them stick around in case anything goes wrong during the 7:00 news, and 11:00? And if anything happens during the 4:30–7 a.m. news, the station can call Alex at home and have them bop over and fix the problem. Oh, and also the news at noon, and the 4 p.m. block.

不同观点：
• **boznz 的观点**：自主工作虽然回报丰厚，但on-call的压力非常大，尤其是在特定时间段内需要全天候待命，导致个人时间和休息时间被侵占。他提到在高压环境下容易犯错，并且由于独自工作，所有责任都落在他一人身上。
• **dadkins 的观点**：提倡采用轮班制，像某些SRE岗位那样明确披露夜班需求，而不是让员工在正常工作之外还要承受随时待命的压力。这种透明的安排比让员工在正常工作之外待命更合理。
• **Animats 的观点**：在加州等地区，on-call时间实际上是需要支付“待命时间”工资的。他引用了相关法律案例，指出在工会化的工作中，on-call员工通常会获得额外的报酬和最低工时保障。
• **yodsanklai 的观点**：on-call是工作中最糟糕的部分，尤其是在系统质量无法控制且没有明确所有权的情况下，问题往往被推给下一个on-call的人，导致恶性循环。
• **nhumrich 的观点**：认为on-call的问题往往是自找的，比如系统不够健壮或警报设置不合理。他主张通过改善系统来减少on-call的必要性，而不是通过支付额外报酬来解决问题。
• **purplejacket 的观点**：建议通过高额的财务激励来补偿on-call工作，例如在非工作时间以10倍正常工资支付on-call工作。这种做法可以促使公司优化on-call流程，只处理最重要的问题。
• **Artooooour 的观点**：在其所在国家，on-call的加班是有明确报酬的，员工可以选择是否接受额外工时，且公司从未在支付方面出现问题。
• **staplung 的观点**：on-call制度存在缺陷，因为它实际上鼓励员工尽量减少on-call工作的时间，而不是去解决根本问题。这导致了一种恶性循环，员工为了完成主要任务而忽视on-call职责。
• **smackeyacky 的观点**：回忆起90年代的“呼叫疯狂”经历，起初觉得on-call是一种责任的提升，但很快发现这是一种束缚。
• **mjcarden 的观点**：由于on-call的压力，他在2023年年中辞职，经过六个月才恢复到健康状态。现在的工作没有on-call的安排，待遇更好。
• **srhtftw 的观点**：on-call制度混淆了角色和责任，剥夺了开发人员的资源，最终导致倦怠。应尽快结束这种做法，以改善行业状况。

补充讨论：
• **neilv 的观点**：提到管理层在处理on-call压力时可能存在的失误，例如没有与员工沟通其困扰，并指出某些文章可能对作者有宣泄作用，但其中也包含了一些可操作的建议。同时，引用了《Soul of a New Machine》一书，反映了项目中的艰难过程。

争议焦点：
• on-call工作是否应获得额外报酬以及如何设计合理的补偿机制。
• 是否应通过改善系统和流程来减少on-call的必要性，还是通过透明的轮班制来解决on-call的压力问题。
• 员工在on-call过程中面临的责任和压力如何平衡，尤其是在系统质量无法控制的情况下。

An HTTP Server in Go From scratch: Part 2
Follow along while I improve the HTTPServer I wrote from scratch in Go.
March 2025
Last year I wrote a
blog post
explaining how I built my HTTP Server in Golang by following a
Coder Crafters
, I got some good feedback on it and improved the HTTP Server quite a bit, let’s dive into the changes!
The
git repository
is still available if you want to look at the whole codebase.
The first unit test
Let’s start by adding a unit test, I was relying on the Codecrafters test suite but now I want to have some of my own unit tests.
This should mimic the first stage of the Codecrafters test suit:
func
TestServerStart
(t
*
testing.T) {
// Start the server
router
:=
server.
NewServer
()
go
router.
Start
()
// Give the server a moment to start
time.
Sleep
(
100
*
time.Millisecond)
// Not the most robust, good enough to start
// Try to connect to the server
conn, err
:=
net.
Dial
(
"tcp"
,
"localhost:4221"
)
if
err
!=
nil
{
t.
Fatalf
(
"Could not connect to server:
%v
"
, err)
}
defer
conn.
Close
()
t.
Log
(
"Successfully connected to the server"
)
}
Fixing issues found by readers
Headers should be case-insensitive and accept multiple values
A Reddit comment mentioned that headers should be case-insensitive, and that some of them could have multiple values. That means that my naive
Headers map[string]string
is not correct!
After reading the Golang doc for the HTTP package, I ended up with this:
type
Header
map
[
string
][]
string
// this is now an array of strings
func
(header Header)
Get
(key
string
)
string
{
if
values, ok
:=
header[strings.
ToUpper
(key)]; ok
&&
len
(values)
>
0
{
return
values[
0
]
// get only returns the first value! To get all values, .Values() should be used
}
return
""
}
func
(header Header)
Set
(key
string
, value
string
) {
header[strings.
ToUpper
(key)]
=
[]
string
{value}
// I always use ToUpper when interacting with the headers
}
func
(header Header)
Add
(key
string
, value
string
) {
header[strings.
ToUpper
(key)]
=
append
(header[strings.
ToUpper
(key)], value)
}
Instead of using
toUpper
I could have used
textproto.CanonicalMIMEHeaderKey(s)
but it felt like cheating a bit in this “from scratch” serie, and I did not want to implement it myself today!
I’m also adding a second test to check that I’m correctly parsing the request.
func
TestParseRequest
(t
*
testing.T) {
rawRequest
:=
"GET /index.html HTTP/1.1
\r\n
"
+
"Host: www.example.com
\r\n
"
+
"User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/91.0.4472.124 Safari/537.36
\r\n
"
+
"Content-Length: 3
\r\n
"
+
"
\r\n
"
+
"abc"
request, err
:=
parseRequest
([]
byte
(rawRequest))
if
err
!=
nil
{
t.
Errorf
(
"Expected no error, got
%s
"
, err)
}
if
request.Method
!=
"GET"
{
t.
Errorf
(
"Expected method GET, got
%s
"
, request.Method)
}
if
request.Url.Original
!=
"/index.html"
{
t.
Errorf
(
"Expected path /index.html, got
%s
"
, request.Url.Original)
}
if
request.Headers.
Get
(
"Host"
)
!=
"www.example.com"
{
t.
Errorf
(
"Expected Host header www.example.com, got
%s
"
, request.Headers[
"Host"
])
}
expectedUserAgent
:=
"Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/91.0.4472.124 Safari/537.36"
if
request.Headers.
Get
(
"User-Agent"
)
!=
expectedUserAgent {
t.
Errorf
(
"Expected User-Agent header
%s
, got
%s
"
, expectedUserAgent, request.Headers[
"User-Agent"
])
}
if
string
(request.Body)
!=
"abc"
{
t.
Errorf
(
"Expected body
%s
, got
%s
"
,
"abc"
,
string
(request.Body))
}
}
Stream the response instead of sending it as a single string
The next comment mentions that I should allow responses to be a stream (so an io.Writer in go).
For the most part it’s quite straightforward, and I can simply replace every instance of
str += "some string"
by
io.WriteString(w, "some string")
.
And pass the connection the the write method:
route.Callback(*request).Write(conn)
Handling bigger payloads
Do you recall this from last post ?
// Not handling bigger payload for now
rawReq
:=
make
([]
byte
,
4096
)
Well, it’s time.
rawReq
:=
make
([]
byte
,
0
)
for
{
// It's gonna hang if requestLength % 4096 == 0
buffer
:=
make
([]
byte
,
4096
)
n, err
:=
conn.
Read
(buffer)
if
n
>
0
{
rawReq
=
append
(rawReq, buffer[:n]
...
)
}
if
n
<
4096
||
err
!=
nil
{
break
}
}
This is another very naive implementation, but it handle bigger payloads for now!
However it breaks if the payload is a multiple of 4096, because there may be nothing left to read, but the loop is still waiting
To fix this issue, I add:
conn.
SetReadDeadline
(time.
Now
().
Add
(
10
*
time.Millisecond))
// ensure the connection is not hanging waiting for data for no reason
I’m pretty sure the correct implementation would be to start parsing the data until I find the content-length to know exactly how much more I should read, but that’s good enough for now!

data.title: Golang on the Playstation 2
data.author: donatj
data.article_summary:
文章主要讲述了作者尝试在PlayStation 2（PS2）上运行自定义代码的经历，特别是使用Go语言进行开发。由于Go默认不支持PS2这种平台，作者转向了TinyGo，一个支持小型设备和嵌入式系统的Go编译器。PS2的CPU是Emotion Engine，基于MIPS R5900架构，而TinyGo虽然支持MIPS-III，但不直接支持R5900。此外，PS2缺乏操作系统，给开发带来更多挑战。

作者提到使用ps2dev SDK来辅助开发，该SDK提供了一些库和工具，但由于ABI（应用二进制接口）的兼容性问题，使得开发过程变得复杂。作者最终通过配置TinyGo目标文件（ps2.json）来生成适合PS2的代码，尽管过程中遇到很多技术难题，如MIPS的N32标准和64位处理器的处理等。

作者计划在未来发布相关代码，并可能尝试完全用Go实现功能，而不仅依赖ps2dev。整个过程充满挑战，但作者乐于探索这种“让设备做 unexpected 事情”的乐趣。

43498481.article_content:
I always wanted to do some weird stuff with consoles. I’m not sure why, but making devices do unexpected things is always an interesting topic for me. And the same applies to the
PlayStation 2
, the 2000 console released by Sony.
Also, Sony, don’t sue me for this lol
Let’s get straight into it: I want to run code into consoles (more on
why
this in a future post). Normally this is done in low(er) level languages, but nowadays we have better and easier to work with languages such as
Go
. So I was wondering.. why not?
Looking online, however, yielded no easy way of doing this, so I decided to tackle this problem myself.
Please note that I’m writing this after a lot of the research here has been done and tested already. This means that a lot of the experimentation here is from memory and from retracing my steps, so there might be inconsistencies here and there.
Also note that this is all running inside an emulator. I do own a PS2 that I can test this, but I’m too lazy to set it up. Plus I want fully functional demos before doing so.
Final note: the code will be released at a later point and I’ll update the post accordingly.
The challenge
By default,
Go only supports a handful of platforms
, and unfortunately that does not include the PS2. In fact, Go seems to require an OS behind the scenes, thing that we don’t even have over there (not considering PS2 Linux). To solve that, however, we have
TinyGo
, a Go compiler for small devices, like microcontrollers and embedded systems. The basic way it works is that it gets the Go code, turns into LLVM IR, and then that into the binary code for whatever target we’re trying to code for.
The PS2 main CPU is called
Emotion Engine
, which is based on a MIPS R5900. It implements the instructions for MIPS-III and MIPS-IV, plus some custom stuff. It also is missing a few other things (more on that later). Go can actually build code for MIPS already, which should save me some time, but not a lot, as I need to get TinyGo to work on it. TinyGo relies on LLVM 19, which does support MIPS-III, but not the R5900 CPU directly.
These are all technical issues. There’s a much more pressing one: I don’t know how the PS2 works.
Well, that should be fun.
The ps2dev SDK and its quirks
If you look it up online for a way of developing code for the PS2, you’ll probably cross paths with
ps2dev
. This is a full-blown SDK that lets you generate binaries for it in a pretty neat way. The coolest thing about it is that it already provides a bunch of libraries for graphical operations, debugging, I/O, etc - even a stdlib is provided! Because of that, I thought: hey, maybe I want to link to their code - this would allow an easier and faster implementation of anything for the PS2 in Go. Think of it as an “OS” API (technically it’s not?), which we could call whenever we want to do things we don’t want to reimplement (or that aren’t even worth trying sometimes).
That said, this introduces a few problems. The first one is that the ps2dev libraries are compiled to the MIPS-III N32 standard. This means that, whatever code we produce, needs to target the same thing. Same hard-float, same N32 ABI, etc. This is a bit annoying, but manageable. The reason why it needs to match is because we’ll be linking our code to their pre-built libraries, and linkers are not really fond of dealing with different targets.
For the sake of clarification: MIPS-III N32 means that this is targeting a MIPS CPU that is implementing the MIPS-III instruction set. This is a 64bit CPU, but due to the N32, this is running 32bit code with some 64bit instructions to handle 64bit integers. This is very confusing, but you can check
this
to read more about it.
Because of this, you’ll see my attempts to target
mipsel
with a
mips3
CPU in the next steps, even though it should, technically speaking, be a
mips64el
, as this is a 64bit CPU. N32 should force things to run in 32bit mode, even though though our target should support 64bit code. However, Clang/LLVM and TinyGo get kinda messy on this and it gets very confusing and complicated. Also, building for
mips64el
caused TinyGo to failed some verification steps when generating code with the LLVM, as well as clang to refuse to properly build it as the code is kinda broken. Since I
really
wanted to move forward, I gave up and opted for generating
mipsel
code with the N32 ABI, which will force clang to change it to a MIPS64 internally, but still generate valid code. Like I said, it’s very weird. Please bear with me, this is all new to me too! :D
Further reiteration on this topic might be necessary to get this just right, but I’m not diving into this hell right now. Future-wise we can try dropping ps2dev and doing things directly in Go, but some assembly is required - literally and metaphorically.
Getting TinyGo to generate some code
For TinyGo to know about a certain target, it requires a file defining it - we’ll call it
ps2.json
. It defines a bunch of very interesting things that we don’t really car
43498481.article_summary:
文章主要讲述了作者尝试在PlayStation 2（PS2）上运行自定义代码的经历，特别是使用Go语言进行开发。由于Go默认不支持PS2这种平台，作者转向了TinyGo，一个支持小型设备和嵌入式系统的Go编译器。PS2的CPU是Emotion Engine，基于MIPS R5900架构，而TinyGo虽然支持MIPS-III，但不直接支持R5900。此外，PS2缺乏操作系统，给开发带来更多挑战。

作者提到使用ps2dev SDK来辅助开发，该SDK提供了一些库和工具，但由于ABI（应用二进制接口）的兼容性问题，使得开发过程变得复杂。作者最终通过配置TinyGo目标文件（ps2.json）来生成适合PS2的代码，尽管过程中遇到很多技术难题，如MIPS的N32标准和64位处理器的处理等。

作者计划在未来发布相关代码，并可能尝试完全用Go实现功能，而不仅依赖ps2dev。整个过程充满挑战，但作者乐于探索这种“让设备做 unexpected 事情”的乐趣。
43498481.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对PS1时代游戏反编译过程的讨论，以及对不同平台和编译器使用的看法。

不同观点：
• [jonhohle] 认为使用GCC作为编译器非常有益，因为GCC工具链在MIPS架构上仍然有效，并且源代码和补丁是开源的。他还提到PS2类似，但PSP使用了MetroWorks编译器，这带来了一些挑战。他认为，只要能够将运行时静态编译进最终二进制文件，GCC（可能还有clang）支持的大多数语言可以 targeting 许多旧系统。

• [pjmp] 对[jonhohle]的工作表示赞赏，并补充提到除了TinyGo之外，还有另一个用于商业产品的裸机Go版本TamaGo。他提供了相关的链接以供进一步参考。

• [nasretdinov] 持不同看法，认为除非每次编译后都能烧录一张在真实硬件上工作的DVD，否则不算真正成功。这暗示了对实际硬件兼容性的重视。

• [rkachowski] 表达了对跳入不熟悉领域进行探索的赞赏，分享了自己在PS2开发中遇到的一些古怪问题的经验，并赞扬了[jonhohle]的工作。

• [djmips] 表示支持，甚至认为可以在游戏开发活动中使用这种方法，鼓励继续努力。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了不同编译器（GCC、MetroWorks、TinyGo、TamaGo）在不同平台（PS1、PS2、PSP、ARM）上的适用性和挑战。
• 争议的焦点在于反编译工作是否真正成功，特别是[nasretdinov]对实际硬件兼容性的严格要求与其他参与者对软件层面的成就的认可之间的对比。
• 提供了关于TamaGo的额外资源链接，这为对裸机Go版本感兴趣的读者提供了深入了解的途径。

总体来看，讨论围绕反编译工作的技术细节、不同编译器的优劣、以及对实际硬件测试重要性的不同看法展开。

data.title: Better Shell History Search
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何通过改进Unix终端中的命令历史搜索功能来提高工作效率。作者指出，许多人未充分利用Shell历史搜索功能，而依赖于上下键查找命令，这降低了效率。作者分享了自己通过结合使用Ctrl-r和工具fzf（以及后来发现的skim）实现更高效的命令搜索体验。这些工具支持模糊搜索和多项显示，大幅提升了作者在终端中的操作效率，并促使他更大胆地使用复杂命令。作者强调，Ctrl-r与fzf或skim的组合是Unix用户的显著生产力提升工具，同时提到Atuin作为更高级的历史记录机制，但未深入采用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： shell历史命令的管理与搜索工具选择

不同观点：
• ackyshake认为使用zsh的交互式注释功能通过标签对命令进行分类，并通过ctrl-r键绑定快速查找命令，无需额外插件，简单高效，且适用于bash和远程系统。
• BeeOnRope推荐使用Atuin进行历史命令同步和管理，但对Atuin的模糊搜索功能不如fzf表示不满，认为其搜索 heuristics 不够有效。
• yb303介绍了自己多年的解决方案，利用bash钩子记录命令历史，包括目录和git分支信息，通过自定义bash函数进行搜索，作为ctrl-r的补充，特别适用于多会话场景。
• kyyol表示自己是Atuin的长期用户，并好奇其他用户使用的shell搜索工具，暗示对Atuin的认可。
• joatmon-snoo提到使用awk时需要注意不同版本之间的差异，曾经在单元测试中遇到不一致的问题，暗示工具版本问题可能带来的困扰。
• doawoo偏好简单的alias hst="history | fzf"方案，强调简单带来的满足感，不追求过多功能。
• 7e指出该讨论是重复的，并给出之前讨论的链接，隐含对论坛内容管理的不满。
• wonger_提到使用fzf/skim进行相对时间戳的管理，并指出选择skim作为fzf替代品的一些理由，暗示Atuin和fish等工具的一些不足。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对工具的复杂性和功能丰富度有不同偏好，有人喜欢简单有效的方案（如doawoo和ackyshake），有人则喜欢功能更全面的工具（如BeeOnRope和kyyol对Atuin的讨论）。
• 版本兼容性问题（如joatmon-snoo提到的awk版本问题）在选择和使用工具时需要注意。
• 一些用户（如wonger_）提到工具替代品（如skim替代fzf），为其他用户提供了更多选择参考。
• 总体上，讨论围绕着历史命令管理工具的选择和自定义方案，展现了不同工具的优缺点及用户偏好。

I spend an awful lot of my day in Unix terminals running shell commands. For
some reason, the variance in efficiency between different people when using the shell
is huge: I know people who can run rings around me, and Iâve come across
more than one paid professional who doesnât use the âupâ key to retrieve the
previous command.
I chose that last example very deliberately: most of the commands most of us
run in the shell are highly repetitive. I typically run around 50-100 unique
(i.e. syntactically distinct) shell commands per working day
[1]
â but
Iâll often run a tiny subset of those commands (e.g.
cargo test
) hundreds of
time in a single day.
Since many command-line tools have hard-to-remember options, we can save huge
chunks of time â not to mention make fewer errors â if we can search our
shell history to find a previous incantation of a command we want to run. In
this post Iâm going to show how, with little effort, searching shell
history can look like this:
[Video]
Searching shell history
Larger Unix shells such as Bash have long allowed users to search through their
shell history by pressing
Ctrl-r
and entering a substring. If I (in order)
executed the commands
cat /etc/motd
then
cat /etc/rc.conf
, then
Ctrl-r
followed by âcatâ will first match
cat /etc/rc.conf
; pressing
Ctrl-r
again
will cycle backwards for the next match which is
cat /etc/motd
. I almost
never used this feature, because substring matching is too crude.
For example, I may know the command I want is
cat
, the leaf
name Iâm looking for is
motd
but I donât remember the directory: substring
matching canât help me find what Iâm looking for. Instead, I regularly used
grep
(with wildcards) to search through my shellâs history file instead.
For me, the game changer was pairing
Ctrl-r
with
fzf
, which brought two changes. First,
matching is âfuzzyâ, so I can type âc moâ and
cat /etc/motd
will be
matched. Second, multiple matches are shown at once. Typing âcatâ will show
me several
cat
commands, allowing me to quickly select the right
incantation (which may not have been the most recent).
Itâs difficult for me to overstate how powerful a feature this is. Few things
in life make me as happy as pressing
ctrl-R
then typing â
l1
â and having a 100
character command-line execution that runs a complicated debugging tool, with
multiple environment variables set, whose output gets put in
/tmp/l1
appear
in my terminal.
Using
Ctrl-r
and fzf roughly doubled my efficiency in the shell
overnight. Interestingly, it had an even greater long term effect: I became a
more ambitious user of shell commands because I knew I could outsource my
memory to fzf. For example, since itâs now very easy to recall past commands, I
no longer set global environment variables, which had previously caused me
grief when I forgot about them
[2]
. Now I set environment variables on a
per-command basis, knowing that I can recall them with
Ctrl-r
and fzf.
For many years my favoured shell was zsh. When I later moved from zsh to fish,
Ctrl-r
and fzf was the first thing I configured; and when I moved back to zsh
[3]
, and redid my configuration from scratch,
Ctrl-r
and fzf was again the first
thing I got working (shortly followed by
autosuggestions
). If you
take nothing else from this
post than â
Ctrl-r
and fzf are a significant productivity boon for Unix
usersâ, then I will have done something useful.
No tool, of course, is perfect. A
couple of months back I somehow stumbled across
skim
, an fzf-alike that out-of-the-box
happens to suit me just a little bit better than fzf. The differences
are mostly minor, and you wonât go far wrong with either tool. That said,
I find that skimâs matching more often finds the commands I want quickly,
I prefer skimâs UI, and I find it easier to install skim on
random boxes â small advantages, perhaps, but enough for switching to be
worth it for me.
Doing even better
Finding Skim encouraged me to quickly look around to see what else in this sphere might
improve my productivity. I quickly came across
Atuin
, which is a much
more sophisticated shell history recording mechanism: the video on its front
page showed a much nicer matching UI than I had previously considered possible.
However, I quickly realised Atuin wasnât for me or, at least, wasnât easily for
me.
