data.title: How I pwned a major New Zealand service provider
data.author: MrBruh
data.article_summary: 2025年2月19日，一名安全研究人员在测试新西兰一款名为KiwiServices的应用程序时，发现其用户数据库存在严重漏洞。通过篡改HTTP请求参数，研究人员能够访问其他用户的信息，可能导致整个数据库泄露。研究人员遵循负责任的披露政策，于2月20日向公司报告了该问题。公司确认问题后，于3月11日修复了漏洞，并于3月22日结束了30天的披露期。3月25日，研究人员发布了此次事件的详细报告。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络安全漏洞的披露及处理方式，特别是在澳大利亚和新西兰的数据安全问题

不同观点：
• [taitems] 认为尽管存在漏洞，但至少相关方曾经关注过漏洞。他提到在澳大利亚的一个推荐服务中发现可以通过电话号码枚举获取大量个人信息，并已经多次负责任地披露了该漏洞，但LinkedIn联系的员工没有回应，漏洞依然未修复。

• [ngonch] 持批评态度，认为澳大利亚和新西兰在处理个人数据方面非常粗心。他分享了自己在一家海滩冲浪板租赁店被要求将信用卡信息（包括CVV）写在纸上的经历，表示震惊。

• [pjsg] 关注API的具体漏洞，质疑该API是否允许通过电话号码枚举用户，并认为如果这是应用程序的第一个API请求且存在严重漏洞，那么整个API可能存在更多问题。

• [girvo] 将问题归因于不良的编程实践，而不是特定的编程语言（如PHP），并指出即便PHP不再流行，类似的漏洞依然存在。

• [hsbauauvhabzb] 警告披露漏洞的人要小心法律风险，指出尽管披露者是出于善意，但仍有可能被视为违法，并提醒有些机构可能会试图将披露者视为坏人。

• [protocolture] 对事件的结局表示乐观，认为相比那些“从未修复漏洞”或“派人追捕披露者”的情况，这个案例的结果还算不错。

• [davesmylie] 提到新西兰Farmers公司最近经历了一次长时间的意外停机，并指出其应用程序评分为4星，暗示可能存在其他技术问题。

• [sitzkrieg] 对API的设计和部署过程表示惊讶，认为设计出这样一个有明显漏洞的API并上线是严重失误。

• [dylan604] 提供技术建议，主张默认情况下对不符合预期的请求返回400错误，以便集中精力确保数据的安全和有效性，并指出未记录的功能可能带来风险。

• [efilife] 关注披露者是否获得报酬，表示希望披露者得到了补偿。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是漏洞披露者是否会面临法律风险，[hsbauauvhabzb]特别强调了这种可能性。
• 另一个讨论点是关于技术实践和API设计的安全性，[pjsg]、[girvo]和[dylan604]都提出了技术上的见解和建议。
• [ngonch] 分享的个人经历引发了对澳大利亚和新西兰数据安全普遍性的讨论。
• 最后，[efilife] 提出了是否支付报酬的问题，这在漏洞披露中也是一个实际的考量。

43466355.article_content:
Note: The name of local company asked very politely to have their name redacted so it has been replaced with KiwiServices as suggested by ChatGPT
Pwning a major New Zealand service provider
On the evening of the 19th February 2025 I had an itch, an itch to do good in the world and to continue to polish my pen testing skills.
First I went through a list of trending apps on the Google Play Store, and looked for an “‘semi” popular app in New Zealand. After a bit of scrolling past the most popular apps I found it, KiwiServices. An app with under a 4 star rating (potentially indicating rushed development) and under 100k downloads.
I did some research and found that the app did infact have a responsible disclosure policy which at that point, I was happy to continue forth.
After downloading the App onto my rooted (spare) phone, I connected it to HTTP Toolkit (shout-out to the creator Tim for giving me free pro) and started the process of creating an account so I could test the different functionalities of the app.
When I typed in my phone number to make an account I noticed it make an outgoing HTTP request checking if I already had an account.
https://kiwiservices.example.com/users?filter=["phone":"64123456789"]
Can you spot the potential issue?
Yes, you just had the same thought as me. If I removed the filter, what would happen? Would it return user details unrelated to my account, or would it just error out?
Well it actually turned out, neither. The request timed out after 30 seconds with no data returned. However this is still very odd as the request should have either given an error code or some kind of response.
My next thought was that what if the request was timing out because it was trying to do a computationally heavy task such as gathering multiple users details and send it to me.
After some trial and error I managed to finally make the request work.
https://kiwiservices.example.com/users?range=[1,1] // Requests the first user
This returned a list of user[s] containing the following data (censored) for what seemed to be a testing account.
[
{
"id": 1,
"email": "example@gmail.com",
"firstName": "John",
"lastName": "Smith",
"phone": "64123456789",
"dateOfBirth": "2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
"firstSeen": "0000-00-00T00:00:00.000Z",
"lastLoggedIn": null,
"Card": null,
"isNew": 0,
"cognitoId": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
"CustomerId": null,
"LoyaltyId": null,
"LoyaltyCard": null,
"RewardsMemberId": null,
"RewardsCard": null,
"isActive": 1,
"referralCode": "",
"fcmToken": null,
"allowTransNotif": 1,
"allowPromoNotif": 1,
"isVip": 0,
"session_id": 0,
"giftcard_id": 0,
"site_id": []
}
]
At this point I was confident that their entire user database was at risk, since a malicious actor could dump the entire user database by iterating through it with a large range. However it was midnight so I decided to report it the next day after I awoke.
Day 2
On day 2 I awoke and began by finding some form of contact details, information was somewhat sparse but I managed to find a phone number. After talking with someone there they said they would talk to one of the big cheeses and get them to call me back.
After maybe 30 minutes a big wig called me back and I ended up sending them a vulnerability report via email including replication steps.
A while after that, I got an email back saying that they managed to replicate the issue and were working on a fix. We also agreed on a 30-day responsible disclosure period.
As of the 22nd of March they have fixed the vulnerability and the 30-day disclosure period has ended.
Timeline
19/02/2025 - Vulnerability Discovered
20/02/2025 - Vulnerability Reported
11/03/2025 - Vulnerability Fixed
22/03/2025 - 30 Day responsible disclosure ends

43466355.article_summary: 2025年2月19日，一名安全研究人员在测试新西兰一款名为KiwiServices的应用程序时，发现其用户数据库存在严重漏洞。通过篡改HTTP请求参数，研究人员能够访问其他用户的信息，可能导致整个数据库泄露。研究人员遵循负责任的披露政策，于2月20日向公司报告了该问题。公司确认问题后，于3月11日修复了漏洞，并于3月22日结束了30天的披露期。3月25日，研究人员发布了此次事件的详细报告。

data.author: k2enemy
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了作者对咀嚼声等特定声音的极端 intolerance，后来得知这是一种叫做“恐音症”（misophonia）的病症。这种状况通常在青春期出现，表现为对某些声音产生无法控制的反感与愤怒。作者从13岁开始对家人咀嚼声产生强烈不适，并采取各种策略躲避这些声音，如戴耳机、避免共餐等，导致社交退缩。2011年，作者读到一篇关于恐音症的报道，首次了解到自己的问题有一个医学名称，虽无治愈方法，但感到释然。经过多年，作者对恐音症的敏感度有所降低，但科学界对该病症的了解仍有限，其成因和分类尚不明确。文章还介绍了恐音症的研究历史，尤其是神经科学家Pawel Jastreboff对该领域早期研究的贡献。

不同观点：

• [thayne] 和 [toomanyrichies] 提供了个人经历，表明这种敏感性在不同年龄阶段的表现可能不同。前者提到自己从幼年就受到影响，而后者分享了如何通过沟通和使用耳机等方法来缓解与家人共进餐时的压力。
• [thenthenthen] 提出了一种极端的解决方案，即通过生活在嘈杂的环境中来“治愈”这种敏感性，而 [comrade1234] 则分享了朋友通过适应环境克服misophonia的经历。
• [derefr] 提出了一种医学假设，认为某些中耳感染可能导致暂时性的misophonia，这可能解释了一些病例的原因。

• 文化差异在吃饭声音接受度上的影响。例如，[zonkerdonker] 提到在一些东亚文化中，吃饭大声被视为对食物的赞赏，因此这些文化中misophonia的发生率可能较低。

• 其他如[bublyboi]提到的机械键盘声音也引发了类似的情绪反应，显示出misophonia可能不局限于吃饭声音。

• 吃饭声音是否应该被视为不礼貌的行为，以及如何在不冒犯他人的情况下提出改善建议。
• misophonia的成因究竟是心理因素还是生理因素，或是两者兼有。

43470493.article_content:
The Unbearable Loudness of Chewing
Jake Eaton
Why do some people find certain sounds intolerable? And why has it taken so long for scientists to get even a preliminary answer?
It’s a teenage rite of passage to explode into rage at your parents. While the usual outburst is sparked by some combination of hormones, insecurity, and authority issues, for me it was a popping sound in my father’s jaw. I first noticed it at the dinner table. Every time he took a bite, the disc of cartilage that cushioned his jawbone would slip out of place and snap back. Chew, click, chew, click. Like a drum, his mouth reverberated the sound, which changed in pitch each time he opened to take a bite. Layered beneath all of this was the wet percussion of normal chewing. The trio — jaw pop, meat squish, fork scraping teeth — became inescapable. And it drove into me, first through my chest, a surprising shock of affront and disgust that then suffused through my whole body. It was the first time I ever got scared that I wasn’t in control of what was inside my own head.
Jul Quanouai
I can’t precisely date this memory, but I was somewhere around the age of 13 when I became unable to tolerate the sound of other people’s mouths. In a world in which everyone eats, my day to day became an obstacle course. I learned to contract the tensor tympani muscle in my middle ear to dampen sounds.  In moments of silence, I was sensitive enough that even the subtle parting of lips could trigger in me the urge to flee. There wasn’t logic to what I felt. I knew that. It changed nothing. In my worst moments I started fights, especially with my family, among whom the condition, whatever it was, felt orders of magnitude more severe.
I learned strategies to hide my aversion. Restaurants and the school cafeteria were loud enough to mask eating sounds. You couldn’t eat in my car — it was, I said, just a cleanliness thing. I wore headphones everywhere. Still, I felt the consequences. I became more introverted. My family resigned to eating dinner with the TV on. My high school girlfriend called me out on what had become my habitual death stare when we ate near each other. I fell out with my best friend after I questioned his family’s table manners. I spent hours alone trying to integrate whatever was happening as
part of me
, hoping I had a wire crossed, afraid that I was experiencing — there was nothing online to help me — an incipient slide into mental illness.
And then in 2011, my first year out of college, I happened upon a piece in the
New York Times
which described a poorly understood condition some scientists had begun to call misophonia.
1
For its sufferers, certain sounds — often chewing — evoked what seemed an uncontrollable and disproportionate reaction of anger and disgust. It consistently appeared in adolescence. It had no cure. It was, or at least one neuroscientist hypothesized, a hard-wired condition, “a ‘physiological abnormality’ that resides in brain structures activated by processed sound.”
Awash in the relief of diagnosis — not vindication so much as no longer feeling alone — the first thing I did was forward the article to my family. “So please be sensitive toward my ‘physiological abnormality’ when I come home,” I wrote, shielding my sincerity in irony.
13 years later, I feel much less impacted by misophonia. My family knows what it is, even if they don’t fully understand it. In this, they aren’t much different than the general public. But it’s only after spending a few months reading and speaking to researchers that I’ve come to realize that the science of misophonia — at least in what we can say with certainty — isn’t well established either.
It has taken, in fact, more than 20 years since the condition was first recognized to even arrive at a definition. And outside of that, some of the most basic questions remain up for debate. Where does misophonia originate, and why? Is it a medical disorder, a neurological disorder, a psychiatric disorder, or something else entirely? Most important of all — at least to the millions of people who likely suffer from it, many without fully understanding what it is — can it be cured?
Starting conditions
In 1983, Pawel Jastreboff, a Polish engineer-turned-neuroscientist, began studying tinnitus. One of his main contributions from his early research was an animal model of the condition. It was a clever experiment that built on the work of his Ph.D. advisor, Jerzy Konorski, who developed the idea of operant conditioning after working in Ivan Pavlov’s lab.
Jastreboff raised rats to live with a constant, high-pitched ringing sound. They were then trained to expect a mild electric shock when the sound shut off. Next, he gave the rats salicylate (aspirin), which is known to cause ringing in the ears. And then he watched how the rats behaved when he shut off the tone. Rather than behave as if it was silent and a shock was coming, they acted normally. It appeared they were still hearing a ringing. While the model

data.title: LibreOffice downloads on the rise as users look to avoid subscription costs
data.author: cable2600
data.article_summary: LibreOffice的下载量持续上升，每周接近100万次，达到自2023年以来的最高点。这款免费开源的微软Office替代品由The Document Foundation管理，最新版本25.2发布后下载量进一步增加。相比之下，Apache的OpenOffice则逐渐失去吸引力。LibreOffice尤其受不想支付订阅费的用户青睐，其用户估算约2亿，主要为Windows用户，且在企业和政府中也开始获得关注。尽管存在云版本，The Document Foundation仍专注于桌面版，并表示不会集成AI功能，但鼓励开发者创建负责任的AI扩展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对各类办公软件的评价与选择偏好

不同观点：
• [baq] 认为目前的电子表格软件在处理简单计算和少量查找函数时表现不佳，对性能有较高要求。

• [russnes] 希望更多人使用LibreOffice，以避免因格式不兼容导致的文档问题。
• [vunderba] 强调偏好拥有永久使用权的软件，不喜欢订阅模式，并列举了一些替代专业软件的例子。
• [croes] 认为像Word和LibreOffice这样的程序对大多数人来说过于复杂，尤其是对文本简单右对齐的操作。

• [jmclnx] 表示不常使用办公软件，LibreOffice在处理电子表格时表现足够好。
• [tombert] 是LaTeX用户，认为LibreOffice足够好用，虽然Excel可能略胜一筹，但LibreOffice的性价比高，同时个人偏好OpenOffice的图标。
• [nilram] 使用OpenOffice多年，尚未切换到LibreOffice。
• [PeterStuer] 认为MS Office每次新版本的更新并不总是为了提高实际工作效率，且对手机用户的偏重令人不满。
• [donatj] 质疑现代办公套件的必要性，认为Google Docs足以满足大多数需求。
• [apexalpha] 需要与MS Office兼容的办公软件，认为OnlyOffice比LibreOffice更好，并询问其他可能的选择。
• [cable2600] 指出LibreOffice支持WordPerfect格式，这在MS Office中已被放弃。

补充讨论：
• 对办公软件性能和兼容性的关注，尤其是对处理大表格和查找函数的需求。
• 对软件使用模式的偏好差异，包括本地存储与云存储、订阅模式与永久许可证。
• 对不同办公软件用户界面的个人偏好，如图标设计。
• 不同办公软件在跨平台和格式兼容性上的表现，特别是对旧格式的支持。

争议的焦点：
• 办公软件的选择和兼容性问题，特别是在团队协作中如何统一软件使用。
• 对订阅模式和软件定价策略的不同看法，反映了用户对软件使用权和成本的关注。

43499860.article_content:
by
Agam Shah
U.S. Correspondent
LibreOffice downloads on the rise as users look to avoid subscription costs
news
Mar 06, 2025
3 mins
Office Suites
Productivity Software
The free open-source Microsoft Office alternative is being downloaded by nearly 1 million users a week.
Credit: 															NiroDesign / Getty Images
Interest in
LibreOffice
, the open-source alternative to Microsoft Office, is on the rise, with weekly downloads of its software package close to 1 million a week. That’s the
highest download number since 2023
.
LibreOffice, which runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS, is a standalone desktop office productivity software that is free to use. Downloads have picked up since The Document Foundation, which manages its development,
released version 25.2 last week
.
It has emerged as the most popular open-source suite, with alternative versions such as Apache’s OpenOffice losing steam. The last version of OpenOffice was released in 2023.
“We estimate around 200 million [LibreOffice] users, but it’s important to note that we respect users’ privacy and don’t track them, so we can’t say for sure,” said Mike Saunders, an open-source advocate and a deputy to the board of directors at The Document Foundation.
There is still noteworthy interest in LibreOffice as a standalone desktop alternative to paid office productivity suites, said Jason Wong, distinguished vice president and analyst at Gartner. “Usually these are clients seeking to keep their on-premises implementation, given that both Microsoft and Google have focused on their cloud offerings,” Wong said.
Cost is a factor for evaluating software suites like LibreOffice, Wong said. “The downside is the additional specialized resources and new skills needed to maintain the [software],” he  said.
Downloads of LibreOffice have been steadily climbing with each new version, Saunders said.
Though LibreOffice has traditionally been a favorite of home users, there’s growing interest in businesses and government, Saunders said. The northern German state of Schleswig-Holstein last year said it would move 30,000 PCs from
Microsoft Office
to LibreOffice.
“The majority of our users — 85% — are on Windows, followed by macOS and then Linux,” Saunders said.
Many desktop Linux distributions pre-install LibreOffice, but it’s unclear how many users that represents.
LibreOffice users typically want a straightforward interface, Saunders said. “They don’t want subscriptions, and they don’t want AI being ‘helpful’ by poking its nose into their work — it reminds them of Clippy from the bad old days,” he said.
There are genuine use cases for generative AI tools, but many users prefer to opt-in to it and choose when and where to enable it. “We have zero plans to put AI into LibreOffice. But we understand the value of some AI tools and are encouraging developers to create … extensions that use AI in a responsible way,” Saunders said.
Although there are cloud-based versions of OpenOffice, The Document Foundation has focused on the desktop version, Saunders said.

43499860.article_summary: LibreOffice的下载量持续上升，每周接近100万次，达到自2023年以来的最高点。这款免费开源的微软Office替代品由The Document Foundation管理，最新版本25.2发布后下载量进一步增加。相比之下，Apache的OpenOffice则逐渐失去吸引力。LibreOffice尤其受不想支付订阅费的用户青睐，其用户估算约2亿，主要为Windows用户，且在企业和政府中也开始获得关注。尽管存在云版本，The Document Foundation仍专注于桌面版，并表示不会集成AI功能，但鼓励开发者创建负责任的AI扩展。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国学者是否会因各种因素（如薪资、学术环境、政治氛围等）离开美国，前往其他国家（如加拿大或欧洲国家）寻找学术工作机会。

不同观点：
• **[mnky9800n]** 认为，尽管有些人讨论离开美国去欧洲或加拿大，但实际愿意这样做的人可能很少。他指出，美国助理教授的薪资较高（约10万美元/年），而欧洲国家（如挪威）的薪资较低（约6.9-7万美元/年），且生活成本高、学术体系不同、语言要求等都是障碍。他认为加拿大因相似的文化和较高的薪资可能成为更具吸引力的目的地，但总体上人们可能只是讨论而不会真的行动。

• **[MattGrommes]** 担心美国正在走向类似二战时德国的道路，即排斥知识分子和科学家。他认为，由于反智主义、政治审查和针对学生移民的严厉政策，美国顶尖知识分子没有理由继续留在美国。

• **[bitsage]** 认为，对于STEM、医学、经济学或法律领域的专业人士来说，移居加拿大或其他国家的机会成本太高，而这些成本对于人文学科的学者来说可能不那么显著。他甚至指出，某些政治团体可能乐见自由派学者离开美国。

• **[1over137]** 提到，加拿大长期以来一直在经历人才外流，这不是由个别教授能改变的，认为需要更多的努力才能逆转这一趋势。

• **[jmclnx]** 表示，如果有机会，自己也会选择离开美国，认为当前的环境不适合顶尖知识分子留在国内。

• **[rufus_foreman]** 引用名言暗示，在当前的危机时刻，只有那些真正忠诚和勇敢的人会继续服务国家，其他人则会退缩。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**在于美国学者是否会因薪资、学术环境、政治氛围等因素实际离开美国。一些人认为大多数人只会讨论而不会行动，而另一些人则认为当前环境确实促使人们考虑离开。

• **薪资和生活成本**是讨论中的重要因素，尤其是美国与欧洲国家之间的薪资差距以及在不同国家生活的成本问题。

• **政治因素**也被多次提到，如反智主义、政治审查和移民政策，这些都被视为推动美国学者考虑离开的重要原因。

• **加拿大的吸引力**在于其相对较高的薪资和相似的文化，但长期人才外流的趋势仍然存在。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对"wrongthink"概念的讨论及其引发的相关议题，包括意识形态控制、多样性声明在学术招聘中的应用以及博物馆的行政管理问题。

不同观点：
• [wombatpm] 引用了"wrongthink"和"doubleplusungood"（来自乔治·奥威尔的《1984》）来暗示某种意识形态控制或思想压制，带有讽刺意味。
• [wrs] 认为相关言论带有苏联时代的风格，暗示某种不加掩饰的俄罗斯（或苏联式）影响。
• [OgsyedIE] 关注于实际问题，询问由美国联邦政府控制的博物馆名单，似乎是在寻求具体信息以进一步了解背景。
• [like_any_other] 认为多样性声明在学术招聘中的应用并非新现象，并提供了多个链接来支持其观点，指出这种做法可能不如传统方式有效，且可能对某些候选人不利。
• [MollyGodiva] 强调史密森学会（Smithsonian）不属于行政部门，因此特朗普政府无权直接干预，但暗示博物馆可能会自愿配合某些政策，可能对其自身造成损害。
• [bediger4000] 认为"不当意识形态"是"觉醒文化"（woke）的委婉说法，并指出其中的讽刺意味。
• [archagon] 引用了一项行政命令，讨论了关于种族是社会构建而非生物现实的展览内容，并担忧这种观点可能导致种族隔离的回归，同时提供了一个NPR链接以支持其担忧。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是意识形态控制和思想自由的界限，尤其是通过"wrongthink"和多样性声明等手段进行潜在的思想审查。
- 另一个焦点是博物馆和学术机构在政治和意识形态影响下的自主性和独立性问题。
- 多样性声明在招聘中的应用及其可能的有效性和公平性也是讨论的重要内容，特别是对不同背景候选人的影响。
- 最后，种族作为生物现实还是社会构建的问题引发了对未来政策走向的担忧和讨论。

data.title: Alibaba Qwen2.5-Omni-7B: Open Source End-to-End Multimodal AI Model
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 阿里巴巴云推出Qwen2.5-Omni-7B，这是一款具备全面多模态感知能力的端到端模型，能够处理文本、图像、音频和视频等多种输入，并生成实时文本和自然语音响应。该模型尽管仅有70亿参数，但性能卓越，适用于手机和笔记本等边缘设备。其创新架构包括Thinker-Talker架构、TMRoPE位置嵌入技术和分块流处理，确保高效的多模态处理和低延迟语音响应。Qwen2.5-Omni-7B已在Hugging Face和GitHub上开源，并已在多个任务中展现出领先的性能，包括语音指令跟随和多模态整合能力。此前，阿里巴巴云还发布了Qwen2.5及其其他版本，进一步推动AI创新。

43496889.article_content:
generated by chat.qwen.ai
By
Crystal Liu
|
Published on March 27, 2025
Alibaba Cloud has launched
Qwen2.5-Omni-7B
, a unified end-to-end multimodal model in the Qwen series. Uniquely designed for comprehensive multimodal perception, it can process diverse inputs, including
text, images, audio, and videos,
while generating
real-time text and natural speech responses
. This sets a new standard for optimal deployable multimodal AI for edge devices like mobile phones and laptops.
Despite its compact 7B-parameter design, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B delivers uncompromised performance and powerful multimodal capabilities. This unique combination makes it the perfect foundation for developing agile, cost-effective AI agents that deliver tangible value, especially intelligent voice applications. For example, the model could be leveraged to transform lives by helping visually impaired users navigate environments through real-time audio descriptions, offering step-by-step cooking guidance by analyzing video ingredients, or powering intelligent customer service dialogues that really understand customer needs.
The model is now
open-sourced on
Hugging Face
and
GitHub
, with additional access via
Qwen Chat
and Alibaba Cloud’s open-source community ModelScope. Over the past years, Alibaba Cloud has made over 200 generative AI models open-source.
High Performance Driven by Innovative Architecture
Qwen2.5-Omni-7B delivers
remarkable performance
across all modalities
, rivaling specialized single-modality models of comparable size. Notably, it sets a new benchmark in
real-time voice interaction, natural and robust speech generation, and end-to-end speech instruction following
.
Its efficiency and high performance stem from its
innovative architecture
, including
Thinker-Talker Architecture
,
which separates text generation (through Thinker) and speech synthesis  (through Talker) to minimize interference among different modalities for high-quality output;
TMRoPE (Time-aligned Multimodal RoPE)
, a position embedding technique to better synchronize the video inputs with audio for coherent content generation; and
Block-wise Streaming Processing
, which enables
low-latency audio responses
for seamless voice interactions.
Outstanding Performance Despite Compact Size
Qwen2.5-Omni-7B was
pre-trained on a vast, diverse dataset
, including
image-text, video-text, video-audio, audio-text, and text data
, ensuring robust performance across tasks.
With the innovative architecture and high-quality pre-trained dataset, the model excels in
following
voice command
, achieving performance levels comparable to pure text input. For tasks that involve integrating multiple modalities, such as those evaluated in
OmniBench
– a benchmark that assesses models’ ability to recognize, interpret, and reason across visual, acoustic, and textual inputs – Qwen2.5-Omni achieves state-of-the-art performance.
Qwen2.5-Omni-7B also demonstrates high performance on robust
speech understanding and generation
capabilities through in-context learning (ICL). Additionally, after reinforcement learning (RL) optimization, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B showed significant improvements in generation stability, with marked reductions in attention misalignment, pronunciation errors, and inappropriate pauses during speech response.
Alibaba Cloud unveils Qwen2.5 last September and released
Qwen2.5-Max
in January, which was ranked 7
th
on Chatbot Arena, matching other top proprietary LLMs and demonstrates exceptional capabilities. Alibaba Cloud also open-sourced
Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen2.5-1M
for enhanced visual understanding and long context input handling.

data.article_summary: 《明镜》周刊报道称，美国总统特朗普的重要安全顾问的私人联系方式，包括手机号码、电子邮件地址，甚至密码，可以通过商业搜索引擎和网上泄露的数据获取。受影响的官员包括国家安全顾问Mike Waltz、国家情报总监Tulsi Gabbard和国防部长Pete Hegseth。这些信息仍在使用，并与Instagram、LinkedIn等社交媒体以及Signal、WhatsApp等通讯应用关联。报道还揭示，这些高层官员曾在Signal聊天群中讨论军事打击，包括对也门胡塞武装的打击计划，且《大西洋》杂志主编被加入该群。虽然特朗普称讨论未涉密，但此类信息泄露可能被敌对情报机构利用，安装间谍软件，获取通讯内容。

U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth: His contact info could be found using a commercial people finder.
Foto: Annabelle Gordon / AFP
Private contact details of the most important security advisers to U.S. President Donald Trump can be found on the internet. DER SPIEGEL reporters were able to find mobile phone numbers, email addresses and even some passwords belonging to the top officials.
To do so, the reporters used commercial people search engines along with hacked customer data that has been published on the web. Those affected by the leaks include National Security Adviser Mike Waltz, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.
Most of these numbers and email addresses are apparently still in use, with some of them linked to profiles on social media platforms like Instagram and LinkedIn. They were used to create Dropbox accounts and profiles in apps that track running data. There are also WhatsApp profiles for the respective phone numbers and even Signal accounts in some cases.
As such, the reporting has revealed an additional grave, previously unknown security breach at the highest levels in Washington. Hostile intelligence services could use this publicly available data to hack the communications of those affected by installing spyware on their devices. It is thus conceivable that foreign agents were privy to the Signal chat group in which Gabbard, Waltz and Hegseth discussed a military strike.
Numbers Linked to Signal Accounts
It remains unclear, however, whether this extremely problematic chat was conducted using Signal accounts linked to the private telephone numbers of the officials involved. Tulsi Gabbard has declined to comment. DER SPIEGEL reporting has demonstrated, though, that privately used and publicly accessible telephone numbers belonging to her and Waltz are, in fact, linked to Signal accounts.
The U.S. newsmagazine
The Atlantic
revealed on Monday that Gabbard, Waltz and Hegseth, along with CIA Director John Ratcliffe and additional officials, discussed an imminent military strike against the Houthi militia in Yemen in a Signal chat. The information shared among the participants included intelligence information and precise attack plans. According to the
Atlantic
, Waltz added the editor-in-chief of the magazine, Jeffrey Goldberg, to the chat group. Precisely why he did so remains unclear.
The White House confirmed the scandal after the fact. Trump insisted that it did not include classified content, a question that is of particular relevance since members of the U.S. government are not permitted to share such information over Signal. The U.S. special envoy for Ukraine and the Middle East, Steve Witkoff, was even in Russia while participating in the chat group.
Bild vergrößern
Pete Hegseth's WhatsApp profile photo
Foto: Screenshot / DER SPIEGEL
DER SPIEGEL was able to find some of the contact information for Gabbard, Hegseth and Waltz in commercial databases, while other information was in so-called password leaks, which are hardly a rarity on the internet. One example is the 2019 discovery by Troy Hunt, who found 773 million email addresses and more than 21 million passwords in a hacker forum.
Since then, there have been numerous additional leaks. Criminals are constantly compiling new collections from hacks, usually to sell them on forums.
It was particularly easy for DER SPIEGEL reporters to discover Hegseth’s mobile number and email address. They turned to a commercial provider of contact information that is primarily used by companies for sales, marketing and recruitment.
DER SPIEGEL sent the provider a link to Hegseth’s LinkedIn profile and received a Gmail address and a mobile phone number in return, in addition to other information. A search of leaked user data revealed that the email address and, in some cases, even the password associated with it, could be found in over 20 publicly accessible leaks. Using publicly available information, it was possible to verify that the email address was used just a few days ago.
The mobile number provided, meanwhile, led to a WhatsApp account that Hegseth apparently only recently deleted. The profile photo showed a shirtless Hegseth in a baseball cap and necklace. Comparisons with other photos of the U.S. secretary of defense using facial recognition software were able to confirm that the photo on the WhatsApp profile was indeed Hegseth.
Several Passwords in Leaked Database

data.title: A decompilation and port of Sonic Advance 2-a GameBoy Advance game written in C
data.author: bane
data.article_summary: SAT-R/sa2 是一个正在进行的GameBoy Advance游戏《Sonic Advance 2》的反编译和移植项目。该项目旨在将游戏的汇编代码反编译为C语言，并支持多平台编译。目前，项目已成功构建多个版本的游戏ROM，并提取了所有音乐和精灵动画帧。虽然部分内容仍在开发中，但所有汇编代码已手动反编译为C代码，且游戏能够编译为宽屏版本。项目还涉及Chao Garden等子游戏的拆解。社区贡献者积极参与，提供了工具和资源支持。项目文档和指南可在sa2.dev找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GBA Sonic游戏的现代PC移植及其相关技术（如反编译、模拟）在游戏社区中的应用和争议。

不同观点：
• **赞赏现代PC移植和反编译项目**：
  - [rossy]：认为GBA上的Sonic游戏未得到足够关注，值得通过现代PC移植（如Sonic 1 Forever、Sonic Origins）来让更多人体验，并提到PC正成为玩老游戏的理想平台。
  - [Gamemaster1379]：支持反编译和模拟技术带来的游戏现代化和跨平台移植，列举了多个成功案例（如《Ocarina of Time》、《Sonic Unleashed》）。
  
• **对法律风险的担忧**：
  - [msk-lywenn]：担心这些基于反编译的项目可能因使用原始游戏素材（如精灵和背景）而遭遇DMCA下架。建议直接发布反编译工具而不是成品。

• **技术讨论与疑问**：
  - [mikae1]：好奇为何最近反编译项目增多，是否存在技术突破。
  - [hobozilla]：探讨AI在将汇编代码映射回C代码方面的能力。
  - [dpedu]：关注反编译代码中有多少是游戏开发者的原始代码，多少是来自原平台的SDK。
  
• **对游戏公司代码管理的兴趣**：
  - [russellbeattie]：好奇Sega如何管理旧代码库，是否存在可供访问的历史游戏代码和资源库，以及普通开发者能否访问这些资源。

• **怀旧与个人情感**：
  - [nake89]：表达对GBA Sonic游戏的怀旧情感，提到自己仍保留着原始的GBA和游戏卡带。

补充讨论：
• **对代码库中包含版权素材的质疑**：
  - [starkparker]：质疑为何在代码库中包含版权保护的PNG文件，可能引发版权问题。

争议的焦点：
- 反编译和现代移植项目的合法性，尤其是涉及版权素材时如何规避法律风险。

data.title: Using uv and PEP 723 for Self-Contained Python Scripts
data.author: thisdavej
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python脚本中的包管理、HTTP客户端的使用以及新兴工具（如uv）的应用和集成

不同观点：
• [ratorx] 认为Python标准库功能已经非常丰富，对于如HTTP请求这样的基础功能，不应该依赖第三方库。即使标准库文档推荐使用第三方库（如Requests），这仍然显得不必要。
• [skeledrew] 提到虽然不太喜欢Python生态中的"Rust化"趋势，但已经开始使用uv工具，并考虑将项目从conda和poetry迁移到uv。
• [cjs_ac] 对Python生态中的包管理现状表示不满，认为解决方案总是倾向于引入更多的包管理工具，而不是简化问题。个人在家庭项目中只使用Debian仓库中的Python包。

补充讨论：
• [frfl] 询问如何将PEP 723和uv与LSP编辑器结合使用，并分享了一种通过`uv sync`命令获取venv路径的变通方法。
• [alkh] 对uv不重新创建venv除非依赖或Python版本发生变化的特性表示赞赏。
• [stereo] 分享了自己从使用虚拟环境到使用shebang和依赖声明的转变，并指出这对于运行临时脚本特别有用。
• [silvanocerza] 提到Hatch已经有一年左右具备类似uv的功能，认为uv并非独一无二。
• [sorenjan] 提供了在Windows上更方便运行Python脚本的方法，如使用py launcher和设置PATHEXT环境变量。
• [ivh] 分享了使用uv与VScode调试器集成的困难，VScode不尊重shebang而是使用自己认为正确的Python解释器。
• [indigodaddy] 关心uv创建的虚拟环境会存在多久，担心大量脚本会导致大量未使用的venv占用空间。
• [sireat] 指出uv并没有解决如何将自包含脚本分享给不熟悉技术的人（如祖母）的问题，因为接收者需要先安装uv。
• [alanfranz] 分享了一种不需要uv的旧方法，用于处理可编辑的单文件Python脚本，但承认需要定期更新依赖。
• [Titan2189] 提到已经将所有脚本改为包含自己的依赖，但尚未解决如何让PyCharm在执行或调试时通过uv运行脚本的问题。
• [Galanwe] 询问是否可以将类似技巧应用于Jupyter Notebook，以便共享声明其依赖的笔记本。

争议焦点：
• Python标准库是否足够强大以避免使用第三方HTTP客户端库。
• 对于Python生态中的包管理工具激增的不满与适应新工具（如uv）的实际需求之间的矛盾。
• uv工具的独特性及其在不同场景下的适用性，包括与编辑器和IDE的集成问题。

不同观点：

• **[squigg]** 讨论了在使用老旧设备（Roland S760采样器）时，由于MSX接口难以找到，使用DIY连接器和PS/2鼠标替代的经验，并表达了对设备运作原理的新理解。
• **[userbinator]** 提供了有关鼠标和键盘协议的技术背景，指出大多数设备在2014年前是双协议支持，但到2019年开始出现仅支持USB的设备。

• **[dekuNukem]** 和 **[ndiddy]** 讨论了使用主动转换器和被动适配器在老旧设备和现代设备之间进行连接的必要性，并提供了相关技术项目和背景解释。
• **[leohonexus]** 通过DisplayPort和HDMI的例子进一步解释了被动适配器的工作原理，强调了设备内部智能支持的重要性。

• **[wildzzz]** 和 **[jackvalentine]** 表达了对适配器技术实现的惊讶和长期困惑的解答，显示了对技术细节的兴趣和理解。

data.title: Things I would have told myself before building an autorouter
data.author: seveibar
data.article_summary:
本文总结了一位开发者在花费一年时间开发自动布线器（autorouter）后，得出的13个重要经验。以下是核心要点：

1. **熟练掌握A\*算法**：A\*是搜索问题的基础算法，适应性强，效率高，应广泛应用。
2. **语言选择不重要**：优化算法时，重点应放在降低迭代次数上，语言对性能的影响较小。
3. **空间哈希索引优于树结构**：空间哈希索引（Spatial Hash Index）比QuadTree等树结构更高效，能显著提升搜索速度。
4. **空间分区和缓存至关重要**：有效的空间分区和缓存策略比单一算法性能优化更重要，能带来数量级的性能提升。

其他经验还包括如何优化超参数、处理复杂布线问题等。开发者强调，算法设计和数据结构的选择比编程语言对性能的影响更大。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：算法与自动布线工具（autorouters）的应用与优化

不同观点：
• GistNoesis支持蒙特卡罗方法，认为它可以通过牺牲准确性来换取速度，特别是在神经网络训练和复杂算法中，具有在高度嵌套循环中快速提供“足够好”结果的优势。例如，AlphaGo等程序利用蒙特卡罗树搜索可以在短时间内找到较优解。
• bArray对现有的自动布线工具（如FreeRouting）表示不满，指出其在优先级处理、差分对布线、高速信号线处理等方面的不足，并寻求更灵活的规则添加功能。
• n4r9对文章中关于递归算法和BFS/A*搜索算法的描述提出质疑，认为文章忽略了A*作为动态算法可以提前终止搜索的优势，并指出A*在多查询场景下的局限性。
• ChrisGammell对自动布线工具持怀疑态度，更倾向于使用协同创作工具，强调在设计初期迭代的重要性，并对新工具的生态系统整合表示关注。
• amiga386强调算法优化的重要性，认为在算法开发初期可以使用解释型语言，但最终为了性能需要用低级语言重写，并以numpy、TensorFlow为例说明性能优化的重要性。
• Animats指出自动布线中的复杂性在于重新布线和组合问题，并怀念KiCAD曾经拥有的自动布线功能。
• fooblaster对比了数字VLSI和PCB自动布线的问题，认为虽然两者有不同的应用场景，但PCB布线问题依然难以解决。
• dkjaudyeqooe反对文章中对树结构和随机算法的全盘否定，认为在数据分布未知或搜索空间极大的情况下，树结构和随机算法仍然具有价值。
• MrLeap从游戏开发角度出发，支持JS选择并强调优化以加速创意迭代，同时对空间散列结构的经验表示认同。
• xg15反对使用蒙特卡罗方法，认为随机性会增加程序的不确定性和调试难度，主张避免不必要的随机性。
• nine_k强调可视化的重要性，认为通过可视化可以帮助理解问题形状，并选择更优的方法。
• knodi123对工作中无法应用大学中学到的算法表示遗憾，认为实际工作中更多是构建UI组件和REST API。
• kayson对“硬件即代码”持怀疑态度，认为硬件设计必须是图形化的，并指出开放数据集和工具的缺乏以及EDA工具的高成本。
• hyperbrainer简要指出BFS也可以是递归搜索，并总体上对文章表示认可。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的算法包括A*、BFS、蒙特卡罗方法、Jump Point Search等，不同算法在不同场景下的优劣被多方讨论。
• 自动布线工具的现有问题和改进方向被多位评论者提及，特别是对优先级处理、规则添加、高速信号线处理等方面的需求。
• 新工具的生态系统整合和对现有工具的不满是另一个值得注意的讨论点。

争议焦点：
• 蒙特卡罗方法的适用性及其在算法优化中的价值受到不同观点的碰撞。
• A*和BFS在搜索算法中的优劣及适用场景被多方讨论，特别是A*的动态特性和提前终止搜索的能力。
• 自动布线工具在实际应用中的局限性和改进方向是另一个争议焦点。

Important lessons from trying to build the world's fastest autorouter for about a year

I’ve spent about a year working on an autorouter for
tscircuit
(an open-source electronics CAD kernel written in Typescript). If I could go back a year, these are the 13 things I would tell myself:
An intermediate stage of our autorouting routing a keyboard.
1. Know A* like the back of your hand, use it everywhere
If I was king for a day, I would rename A* to “Fundamental Algorithm”. It is truly one of the most adaptable and important algorithms for _any kind_ of search. It is simply the best foundation for any kind of informed search (not just for 2d grids!)
Here’s an animated version of A* versus “breadth first search” on a 2d grid:
The way A* explores nodes is a lot faster and more intuitive. The major difference between these two algorithms is BFS explores all adjacent nodes, while A* prioritizes exploring nodes that are closer to the destination. Because it considers a metric outside the graph (the distance to the destination) it’s an
informed search
.
You are already either using BFS or DFS (depth-first search) in your code.
A recursive algorithm is a depth first search. Any loop that explores candidates/neighbors without sorting the candidates is a BFS.
99% of the time you can convert it to A* and get dramatic performance gains!
One of my favorite techniques in our autorouter is we run multiple levels of A* to discover the optimal hyperparameters for a particular problem. So we’re basically running each autorouter as a candidate, then using A* to determine which autorouters we should spend the most time on!
See all those numbers at the top? Those are each different configurations of hyper parameters. Running each autorouter fairly would be a huge waste of time- if one autorouter starts to win (it is successfully routing with good costs) allocate more iterations to it! This kind of meta-A* combines a regular cost function that penalizes distance with a cost function that penalizes iterations.
2. Implementation Language doesn’t matter
I’m controversially writing our autorouter in Javascript. This is the first thing people call out, but it’s not as unreasonable as you might expect. Consider that when optimizing an algorithm, you’re basically looking at improving two things:
Lowering the number of iterations required (make the algorithm smart)
Increasing the speed of each iteration
People focus
way too much
on improving the speed of each iteration. If you are doing something dumb (like converting everything to a grid for overlap testing), Javascript performance will beat you no matter what language you use!
Dumb algorithms in optimal assembly
are still slower than smart algorithm algorithms in Javascript!
Algorithm > Language!
95% of your focus should be on reducing the number of iterations. This is why language doesn’t matter. Whatever gets you to the smartest, most cacheable algorithm fastest is the best language.
3. Spatial Hash Indexing > Tree Data Structures
You can’t walk 5 feet into multi-dimensional space optimization without someone mentioning a QuadTree, this incredible data structure that makes
O(N)
search
O(log(N))
when searching for nearby objects in 2d/3d space.
The QuadTree and every general-purpose tree data structure are insanely slow.
Trees are not an informed representation of your data.
Any time you’re using a tree you’re ignoring an
O(~1)
hash algorithm for a more complicated
O(log(N))
algorithm
Why does Javascript use HashSets and HashMaps by default and every chance it gets?
They’re super super fast.
A Spatial Hash Index is the same concept as a HashMap, but instead of hashing the object we hash it’s location and store it in a Cell (or “bucket of things that are close together”)
Let’s look at how we might replace the QuadTree with a SpatialHashIndex with 20% as much code:
There are many variants of this basic data structure for different types of objects, but they all look pretty similar. We’re basically just creating “buckets” with spatial hashes and filling them with any object that is contained within the cell represented by the spatial hash.
The reason spatial hashes aren’t as popular is you need to be careful about selecting your cell size- this is what makes it an informed algorithm. If your cell size isn’t calibrated well, you’ll end up paying high fixed costs per retrieval. In practice, it’s not that difficult to pick a reasonable cell size.
4. Effective Spatial Partitioning + Caching is 1000x more important than algorithm performance

data.title: Arctic sea ice sets a record low maximum in 2025
data.author: martinpw
data.article_summary: 2025年3月22日，北极海冰面积达到年度最大值，为1433万平方公里，是47年卫星记录中的最低值，低于1981至2010年平均值1564万平方公里。此前低值出现在2017年、2018年、2016年和2015年。海冰最大值出现时间较往年平均晚10天，受气温偏高影响，海冰增长缓慢。整个冬季，圣劳伦斯湾几乎无冰，鄂霍次克海海冰显著减少，仅格陵兰海接近常年水平。白令海冬季前期海冰少，但后期增长使其接近常年水平。

主要讨论点：气候变化的影响、责任与行动

不同观点：
• **技术与财富责任**：[astahlx] 认为黑客和有财富的群体有能力建立全球社区来应对气候崩溃，且对气候问题负有责任，因为他们有能力采取行动但往往选择舒适的生活方式。这种观点强调了掌握资源的人群在气候问题上的责任。
  
• **反馈循环和科学工具**：[gmuslera] 指出暴露更多水面会加剧全球变暖，并提到正反馈循环的可怕性。同时，[singularity2001] 提供了一个科学工具链接，帮助理解海冰变化，强调科学数据的重要性。

• **气候工程与悲观预期**：[wasmainiac] 认为大规模气候工程在十年前就应该实施，且由于经济利益驱动，政府和企业很难被说服采取必要行动。这种观点表达了对实现碳中和的悲观预期。

• **地缘政治与阴谋论**：[jamesblonde] 和 [aoweirji3j] 提到了格陵兰的地缘政治竞争，以及特朗普对格陵兰和加拿大的兴趣，暗示气候变化可能被某些政治人物利用以获取利益。

• **精英责任与现实**：[hdivider] 批评金融精英选择投资污染产业而不是解决气候问题，强调这些人的财富和权力使他们有能力改变现状，但他们选择不作为。

• **数据来源与信任**：[jfengel] 对气候变化信息持怀疑态度，认为需在官方政府网站上看到相关信息才能相信，反映了对信息来源的不信任。

• **测量方法与季节性影响**：[zcar] 提出疑问，认为应以全年平均值而非仅冬季月份来衡量海冰变化，指出冰雪与温度变化之间的复杂关系。

补充讨论：
• **经济利益与气候变化**：[jmclnx] 提到气候变化可能带来新的经济机会，如开放石油田和航道，但会加剧气候问题，讽刺了亿万富翁在此过程中的受益。

• **文化与气候变化**：[tonyhart7] 简单提到俄罗斯人可能会喜欢气候变化带来的影响，暗示不同文化和地区对气候变化的反应和态度可能不同。

Arctic sea ice sets a record low maximum in 2025
WEDNESDAY, MARCH 26, 2025
Arctic sea ice extent appears to have reached its annual maximum on March 22, 2025. This is the lowest maximum in the 47-year satellite record, with previous low maximums occurring in 2017, 2018, 2016, and 2015.
Please note that this is a preliminary announcement. Changing weather or late-season growth could still increase the Arctic sea ice extent. NSIDC scientists will release a full analysis of the 2024 to 2025 Arctic winter sea ice conditions in early April.
Overview of conditions
On March 22, Arctic sea ice likely reached its maximum extent for the year, at 14.33 million square kilometers (5.53 million square miles), the lowest in the 47-year satellite record. This year’s maximum extent is 1.31 million square kilometers (506,000 square miles) below the 1981 to 2010 average maximum of 15.64 million square kilometers (6.04 million square miles) and 80,000 square kilometers (31,000 square miles) below the previous lowest maximum that occurred on March 7, 2017.
This year’s maximum occurred 10 days later than the 1981 to 2010 average date of March 12. The date of the maximum has varied considerably over the years, occurring as early as February 24 in 1987 and 1996 and as late as April 2 in 2010.
Figure 1. Arctic sea ice extent for March 22, 2025, was 14.33 million square kilometers (5.53 million square miles). The orange line shows the 1981 to 2010 average extent for that day.
Sea Ice Index
data.
About the data
— Credit:
National Snow and Ice Data Center
Conditions in context
Low sea ice extent persisted around most of the Arctic during the 2024 to 2025 winter season. Notably, the Gulf of St. Lawrence remained virtually ice free and the Sea Okhotsk had substantially lower sea ice extent than average. Only the East Greenland Sea had near-average extent through the winter. The Bering Sea ice extent was low for much of the season, but growth from late February through late March brought the region closer to average conditions and was the primary contributor to the increase of total Arctic sea ice during March. Temperatures were 1 to 2 degrees Celsius (2 to 4 degrees Fahrenheit) above average in the Arctic and the surrounding seas, which likely slowed the rate of ice growth.
Figure 2. The graph above shows Arctic sea ice extent as of March 22, 2025, along with daily ice extent data for four previous years and the record low year. 2024 to 2025 is shown in blue, 2023 to 2024 in green, 2022 to 2023 in orange, 2021 to 2022 in brown, 2020 to 2021 in magenta, and 2011 to 2012 in dashed brown. The 1981 to 2010 median is in dark gray. The gray areas around the median line show the interquartile and interdecile ranges of the data.

data.title: Anti-Orbit Laser Submarines (2017)
data.author: EA-3167
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在太空战争中，当敌方战舰获得制空权并从高轨道攻击时，防御方如何进行反击。敌方可利用高轨道优势，通过激光、导弹和动能武器自由攻击地面目标。防御方需克服多个挑战，如导弹易被击落、大型火箭发射系统脆弱且易成为目标等。使用核动力潜艇装备激光武器被认为是最后的防线，因其隐蔽性强且不易被探测。然而，防御方在反击中面临巨大困难，包括需要极高的ΔV（速度变化量）才能将武器送入高轨道，且敌方可轻松进行轨道轰炸，削弱防御能力。总之，防御方必须寻找创新的解决方案来对抗占据太空优势的敌军。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于未来可能涉及激光、潜艇、空间战斗等科技的讨论，包括技术可行性、战术应用及潜在问题。

不同观点：
• **ginkgotree**：认为从1000公里外发射激光存在大气衰减、光束瞄准与聚焦困难等问题，且所需功率远超当前热管理技术的能力。虽然认为太空战争有趣，但这个想法已经过时，暗示有更好的技术方案。

• **Full_Clark**：讨论了超空泡超音速潜艇的战术优势和缺陷，指出其在快速撤离战斗区域后留下的尾流可能成为追踪线索，并提到具有强大扫描能力的对手能利用相关原理进行搜索。

• **nopelynopington**：以幽默方式指出论坛内容多样性，从高科技战争讨论到技术适配器问题，表现出对多种话题的兴趣。

• **perihelions**：强调隐形技术在未来太空战争中的重要性，指出通过物理原理可以实现接近零排放的隐形空间物体，并讨论了对抗暗空间物体及隐形武器的困难。

• **ranger207**：引用虚构作品《Battletech》中的例子，描述了一种类似概念的潜艇，在故事中成功躲避追捕多年，暗示虚构作品中的概念有时可以启发现实技术讨论。

• **master_crab**：以幽默方式表达对讨论主题的复杂性感到困惑，暗示讨论涉及的物理问题非常复杂。

• **tiku**：提出关于使用遥控飞艇作为无人机平台的想法，建议使用氢气作为浮升和燃料来源，讨论与主要话题有一定偏离。

• **MrBuddyCasino**：提出多个技术问题，包括是否可以使用伸缩式装置减少激光在水中的能量损失，以及讨论水下保护对激光和动能武器的有效性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于激光技术在未来战争中的实际应用及其技术限制，包括大气衰减、光束聚焦、功率需求及热管理等方面。
• 讨论还涉及隐形技术在太空战争中的重要性及其实现方式，以及如何对抗隐形目标。
• 潜艇战术中的尾流问题及其可能导致的追踪风险也被提及，作为对未来战争中潜艇战术的一种思考。
• 虚构作品中的技术概念被引用来说明可能的现实应用，这增加了讨论的趣味性与广泛性。

43499755.article_content:
Laser-equipped nuclear-powered submarines are the perfect last line of defense against an attacking force in orbit.
The situation
You don't win every fight. Eventually, there will come a time in space warfare where a fleet of space warships has defeated all your mobile forces and your immobile defenses. They will bear down on you from above with lasers, missiles and kinetic projectiles and you will have to find a way to prevent their forcing of an unconditional surrender.
We will refer to the opponents as the 'attackers' and to you as the 'defenders'. The first step to devising an effective defense is to understand the situation.
So what is the situation?
Its an enemy ship.
An attacking warship will start out in high orbit. This is an altitude of 2000km or above. Whether it has just arrived from an interplanetary voyage or has recently destroyed your remaining warships, it will go to high orbit to maximize the effectiveness of its space superiority. Space superiority, borrowing from the term 'air superiority', is when a force has complete dominance over all the orbits around a planet. No space-borne forces can oppose this superiority and no reserve forces can challenge them without being quickly destroyed.
What does losing space superiority mean for defenders
?
The most important consequence is that enemy warships have free reign to change orbits, maneuver into favorable positions and receive re-supplies. Their mobility is unconstrained.
High Elliptic Orbits and gravity assists from a large moon allow for a huge variety of orbits.
Attackers in high orbit can make optimal use of their laser weaponry. They can get clear lines of sight onto any spot on the surface, and the long distances between objects forces travel times to lengthen with the secondary effect of giving lasers plenty of time to shoot down targets. Laser effectiveness is generally dependent on how far they are from a target and how much 'dwell time' a beam can spend on a target.
De-orbiting objects from high altitude is inexpensive in terms of deltaV. This works in favour of missiles sent down from orbit by allowing them to use very little propellant to strike ground targets, which makes them lightweight and cheap to send by the hundreds. Additionally, falling towards Earth gives them a big boost to the velocities they achieve before impact.
The same applies to kinetic projectiles, a fact applied in the Rods From God concept of orbital bombardment.
Retaliating
So you want to shoot back at the attackers.
U.S. Army’s Homing Overlay Experiment
Missiles can do the job. They are currently our only method of delivering weapons into orbital space. Something like an ICBM with an additional stage can reach LEO. Reaching higher orbits will require either a very large rocket, a high Isp engine for the upper stage or a launch system such a laser launch or ram accelerator.
However, each of these solutions have major issues when trying to shoot down an opponent in high orbit.
Laser satellite shooting down a missile slowly climbing to orbit.
Large rockets are easy to target and shoot down. A chemical-propellant rocket that needs to minimize its dry mass to achieve the necessary deltaV capacity will have very good acceleration but will end up being very fragile. Nuclear-thermal or nuclear-powered rockets can be much smaller and more durable, but getting sufficient acceleration out of them implies a very high power requirement, which might make them very expensive to throw at the enemy.
Maglev track rocket launch system... vulnerable.
Regular launches take tens of minutes and cannot be disguised from the attackers. Shortening this window of vulnerability can be done by using a launch system that powers the rocket or accelerates it externally. However, the infrastructure for the launch systems will in turn become a priority target for the attackers. Massive, hard to hide and immobile, they will receive a lot of firepower. Some launch systems are practically impossible to shield from damage, such as a laser launch system that needs thousands of exposed laser optics, and others reveal their positions as soon as they fire a rocket. Building underground is also a very expensive endeavour when considering that all the work can be undone by a single 'bunker buster'-type weapon.
The logistics of launching missiles against attackers sitting in orbit works against the defenders. The attackers can de-orbit a missile by expending only a few tens to hundreds of meters per second of deltaV. A defender must equip each missile with tens of thousands of meters per second of deltaV. It might be easier to build more missiles and create rocket fuels on the ground at the start of the war, but after an orbital bombardment campaign by attackers with space superiority, it is unlikely to be the case.

data.title: Every Flop Counts: Scaling a 300B LLM Without Premium GPUs
data.author: bretpiatt
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种在不使用高端GPU的情况下，训练3000亿参数混合专家（Mixture of Experts, MoE）大语言模型（LLM）的方法。作者团队提出了两种模型：Ling-Lite（168亿参数，激活参数27.5亿）和Ling-Plus（2900亿参数，激活参数288亿）。他们通过优化模型架构和训练过程、改进训练异常处理、以及提升模型评估效率，显著降低了训练成本。实验表明，这些模型在性能上可以与同类规模的密集型和MoE模型相媲美，同时在预训练阶段使用较低规格硬件系统可节省约20%的计算成本。该研究为资源受限环境下的AI开发提供了可行的解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于硬件规格和内存使用情况的争议

不同观点：
• flowerthoughts认为文章中没有明确提及硬件规格，仅在表1中提供了有限的信息。他提到六个设备的规格在120-989 TFLOPS和64-96 GB RAM之间，并以RTX 5090为例（约105 TFLOPS）进行比较。

• rahen对表1中300B参数模型的内存使用量表示惊讶。他引用了类似模型（如Llama 3.1和DeepSeek R1）的内存使用数据进行对比，指出Ling模型声称的不到96 GB内存使用量与常规情况不符，质疑是否遗漏了什么信息。

• osti猜测该模型可能是在非NVIDIA GPU的环境下训练的，这可能是导致硬件和内存使用数据差异的原因。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及不同模型之间的参数和内存使用量对比，特别是FP32和FP8精度下的内存需求。
• 对硬件选择的猜测可能影响模型性能和内存使用的理解，强调了硬件环境对模型训练和推理的重要性。
• 争议的焦点在于Ling模型声称的内存使用量是否合理，以及是否存在未说明的硬件或技术优化。

Abstract:
In this technical report, we tackle the challenges of training large-scale Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, focusing on overcoming cost inefficiency and resource limitations prevalent in such systems. To address these issues, we present two differently sized MoE large language models (LLMs), namely Ling-Lite and Ling-Plus (referred to as "Bailing" in Chinese, spelled Bǎilíng in Pinyin). Ling-Lite contains 16.8 billion parameters with 2.75 billion activated parameters, while Ling-Plus boasts 290 billion parameters with 28.8 billion activated parameters. Both models exhibit comparable performance to leading industry benchmarks. This report offers actionable insights to improve the efficiency and accessibility of AI development in resource-constrained settings, promoting more scalable and sustainable technologies. Specifically, to reduce training costs for large-scale MoE models, we propose innovative methods for (1) optimization of model architecture and training processes, (2) refinement of training anomaly handling, and (3) enhancement of model evaluation efficiency. Additionally, leveraging high-quality data generated from knowledge graphs, our models demonstrate superior capabilities in tool use compared to other models. Ultimately, our experimental findings demonstrate that a 300B MoE LLM can be effectively trained on lower-performance devices while achieving comparable performance to models of a similar scale, including dense and MoE models. Compared to high-performance devices, utilizing a lower-specification hardware system during the pre-training phase demonstrates significant cost savings, reducing computing costs by approximately 20%. The models can be accessed at
this https URL

What it takes to add a new backend to Futhark
Posted on March  4, 2025
Recently Scott Pakin
suggested writing a blog post on how to add a
new backend to the Futhark
compiler
, and
since thereâs active fiddling with the backends at this very moment,
this is not a bad idea. Let us manage expectations up front: this will
not be a
tutorial
on adding a backend. I will not go into the deep
details on the specific internal APIs that should be used. Instead, I
will focused on the core representations, and give an idea about the
kind of work (often complicated) and magnitude (sometimes relatively
little) it takes to add a new backend. Itâs also somewhat open
precisely what a âbackendâ even means. Thereâs a significant
difference in complexity between adding a command
futhark foo bar.fut
that produces
something
based on
bar.fut
(very easy), to
implementing another C-like GPU backend (not hard, but you need to
touch a lot of pieces), to creating a fundamentally new backend for an
alien piece of hardware (depending on your needs, can be extremely
challenging).
I will still link pertinent pieces of the source code as applicable -
sometimes it is instructive just how simple (or simplistic) it is to
finally glue together the complex bits. The Futhark compiler currently
supports a fairly diverse set of targets (sequential CPU, multicore,
different GPU APIs, C, Python). To achieve this without undue
duplication of code and effort, the compiler uses fairly heavily
parameterised representations of the program being compiled. Iâll try
to get the gist across, but the full details are very, well, detailed
(and I always feel like they should be simplified - itâs not the
aspect of the compiler weâre most proud of).
For a drier exposition, there is also
the internal compiler
documentation
.
Architectural overview
The Futhark compiler is a monolithic program written in Haskell. All
passes and backends are part of the same executable. In principle, it
would not be too difficult to make it possible to write a backend in a
different language, as a separate executable, although it hasnât been
relevant so far.
The compiler consists of three main parts:
The
frontend
, which is concerned with parsing the Futhark source
language, type-checking it, and transforming it to the core
intermediate representation (IR).
The
middle-end
, which performs gradual refinement,
transformation, and optimisation, on a program represented in
various dialects of the the IR format (more on that below).
The
backend
, which translates from the IR representation into
some lower level representation, such as C - likely via several
steps.
These parts form a chain. The compiler will always run the frontend,
ultimately producing an intermediate representation of the program,
then run an appropriate middle-end
pipeline
, which produces another
representation of the program, and finally pass this to the backend.
The frontend is pretty much the same no matter how you invoke the
Futhark compiler (
futhark c
,
futhark cuda
, etc), but the
middle-end and backend behaves very differently based on the compiler
mode. For example, rather than having a single IR, the compiler
actually has a
family
of IR dialects, suited for different purposes,
and used at different stages of the compiler. To give a gist of what I
mean, consider an extensible Haskell datatype for representing very
simple expressions:

Exp
o
=
Var
String
|
Val
Int
|
Add
(
Exp
o) (
Exp
o)
|
Sub
(
Exp
o) (
Exp

Op
o
Apart from representing variables, values, additions, and
subtractions, this
Exp
type has also has a type parameter
o
that
represents some
other
kind of operation, via the
Op
constructor.
This means we can instantiate a variant of
Exp
that contains, say,
square root as the operation:
data
SqrtOp
=
Sqrt
ExpWithSqrt
type
ExpWithSqrt
=
Exp
SqrtOp
But we could also have one with some general notion of a function call:
data
FunOp
=
Fun
String
[

]
type
ExpWithFun
=

We can now write functions that operate on
Exp o

we parameterise those functions with how to handle the

(using function parameters, type classes, or what have you). This

data.title: Yale professor who studies fascism fleeing US to work in Canada
data.author: 0xmohit
data.article_summary: 耶鲁大学教授杰森·斯坦利（Jason Stanley）是一位研究法西斯主义的学者，因担忧美国政治气候可能使美国走向“法西斯独裁”，决定离开美国，前往加拿大多伦多大学蒙克全球事务与公共政策学院任教。斯坦利特别提到哥伦比亚大学为保联邦资金向特朗普政府妥协的事件，认为学术界对此反应不足。他强调，面对打压，大学应团结抵抗，而非试图避免成为目标。斯坦利还批评了美国教育部关于系统性种族主义教学的新指令，称其将导致“教育独裁”。尽管他希望留在耶鲁与同事共同对抗这些变化，但考虑到孩子成长环境和自身非美国公民身份，他选择移居加拿大。他的决定引发了广泛关注和担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于网络中立性及其废除影响的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持网络中立性废除的观点**：
   - 论据1：废除网络中立性会促进互联网服务提供商（ISP）之间的竞争，因为可以提供差异化的服务。
   - 论据2：网络中立性规定限制了ISP的商业自由，废除后ISP可以自由创新和探索新的商业模式。
   - 例子：一些评论提到，在网络中立性法规出台之前，互联网发展也很好，ISP提供了多种套餐和服务选择。

• **反对网络中立性废除的观点**：
   - 论据1：废除网络中立性会导致大公司掌控互联网，使得小型企业和初创公司处于不利地位，因为它们可能无法负担高额的优先接入费用。
   - 论据2：网络中立性确保了互联网的公平性和开放性，废除将导致互联网变得更像一个“富人游戏”，只有大企业能负担得起更好的服务。
   - 例子：有人提到，网络中立性废除后，可能会出现“快车道”和“慢车道”，导致普通用户的网络体验下降。

• **对竞争环境影响的讨论**：
   - 支持者认为：废除网络中立性将促使更多竞争，因为ISP会根据市场需求调整服务，消费者可以选择最适合自己的服务方案。
   - 反对者认为：废除网络中立性反而会减少竞争，因为大公司可以通过支付更多获得更好的带宽资源，小公司则无法竞争。

• **对政府监管的看法**：
   - 一些人认为政府监管是必要的，以确保互联网的公平和开放。
   - 另一些人认为政府监管往往会阻碍创新，市场自我调节才是最佳途径。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现和现实影响**：
   - 有评论指出，技术上实施网络中立性并不复杂，但废除后可能导致复杂的市场行为，如不同服务级别的定价和质量差异。
   - 也有评论质疑，实际操作中，网络中立性是否真正能够实现其理想化的公平性。

• **对消费者影响**：
   - 支持废除的认为消费者将有更多选择，享受更个性化的服务。
   - 反对废除的则担心消费者将面临更高的费用和不公平的服务质量。

争议焦点：网络中立性的废除是否会促进竞争和创新，还是会导致市场垄断和不公平的互联网接入环境。

Yale professor who studies fascism fleeing US to work in Canada
Jason Stanley, who says grandmother fled Berlin with his father in 1939, says US may become ‘fascist dictatorship’
Rachel Leingang
Wed 26 Mar 2025 18.26 EDT
Last modified on Thu 27 Mar 2025 07.25 EDT
Share
A Yale professor who studies fascism is leaving the US to work at a Canadian university because of the current US political climate, which he worries is putting the US at risk of becoming a “fascist dictatorship”.
Jason Stanley, who wrote the 2018 book How Fascism Works: The Politics of Us and Them, has accepted a position at the University of Toronto’s Munk School of Global Affairs and Public Policy.
Stanley
told the Daily Nous
, a philosophy profession website, that he made the decision “to raise my kids in a country that is not tilting towards a fascist dictatorship”.
He said in an interview that Columbia University’s recent actions moved him to accept the offer. Last Friday, Columbia
gave in
to the Trump administration by agreeing to a series of demands in order to restore $400m in federal funding. These changes include crackdowns on protests, increased security power and “internal reviews” of some academic programs, like the Middle Eastern studies department.
“When I saw Columbia completely capitulate, and I saw this vocabulary of, well, we’re going to work behind the scenes because we’re not going to get targeted – that whole way of thinking pre-supposes that some universities will get targeted, and you don’t want to be one of those universities, and that’s just a losing strategy,” he said.
Stanley added: “You’ve got to just band together and say an attack on one university is an attack on all universities. And maybe you lose that fight, but you’re certainly going to lose this one if you give up before you fight.
“Columbia was just such a warning,” he said. “I just became very worried because I didn’t see a strong enough reaction in other universities to side with Columbia. I see Yale trying not to be a target. And as I said, that’s a losing strategy.”
Stanley said he wasn’t concerned about his ability to continue his scholarship at Yale, but the broader climate against universities played a role. He praised other faculty at Yale for standing up against the attacks on their profession and said he wished he could stay and fight with them.
“But how could you speak out loudly if you’re not an American citizen?” he questioned. “And if you can’t speak out loudly if you’re not an American citizen, when will they come for the American citizens? It’s inevitable.”
Social media posts spread on Wednesday, noting the alarm sounded by a scholar of fascism leaving the country over its political climate. Nikole Hannah-Jones, the journalist and creator of the 1619 Project,
wrote
on the social media platform Bluesky: “When scholars of authoritarianism and fascism leave US universities because of the deteriorating political situation here, we should really worry.”
In a statement, Yale said it remains a “home to world-class faculty members who are dedicated to excellence in scholarship and teaching”.
“Yale is proud of its global faculty community which includes faculty who may no longer work at the institution, or whose contributions to academia may continue at a different home institution,” the university said. “Faculty members make decisions about their careers for a variety of reasons and the university respects all such decisions.”

主要讨论点：关于网络中立性及其废除影响的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持网络中立性废除的观点**：
   - 论据1：废除网络中立性会促进互联网服务提供商（ISP）之间的竞争，因为可以提供差异化的服务。
   - 论据2：网络中立性规定限制了ISP的商业自由，废除后ISP可以自由创新和探索新的商业模式。
   - 例子：一些评论提到，在网络中立性法规出台之前，互联网发展也很好，ISP提供了多种套餐和服务选择。

• **反对网络中立性废除的观点**：
   - 论据1：废除网络中立性会导致大公司掌控互联网，使得小型企业和初创公司处于不利地位，因为它们可能无法负担高额的优先接入费用。
   - 论据2：网络中立性确保了互联网的公平性和开放性，废除将导致互联网变得更像一个“富人游戏”，只有大企业能负担得起更好的服务。
   - 例子：有人提到，网络中立性废除后，可能会出现“快车道”和“慢车道”，导致普通用户的网络体验下降。

• **对竞争环境影响的讨论**：
   - 支持者认为：废除网络中立性将促使更多竞争，因为ISP会根据市场需求调整服务，消费者可以选择最适合自己的服务方案。
   - 反对者认为：废除网络中立性反而会减少竞争，因为大公司可以通过支付更多获得更好的带宽资源，小公司则无法竞争。

• **对政府监管的看法**：
   - 一些人认为政府监管是必要的，以确保互联网的公平和开放。
   - 另一些人认为政府监管往往会阻碍创新，市场自我调节才是最佳途径。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现和现实影响**：
   - 有评论指出，技术上实施网络中立性并不复杂，但废除后可能导致复杂的市场行为，如不同服务级别的定价和质量差异。
   - 也有评论质疑，实际操作中，网络中立性是否真正能够实现其理想化的公平性。

• **对消费者影响**：
   - 支持废除的认为消费者将有更多选择，享受更个性化的服务。
   - 反对废除的则担心消费者将面临更高的费用和不公平的服务质量。

争议焦点：网络中立性的废除是否会促进竞争和创新，还是会导致市场垄断和不公平的互联网接入环境。

data.title: Operationalizing Macaroons
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文主要介绍了Fly.io公司在使用Macaroon安全令牌方面的经验。Macaroon是一种允许用户自行缩小权限范围的承载令牌，类似于JWT，但具有链式HMAC结构，用户可以编辑和分享令牌而不必过于担心安全问题。尽管用户并未充分利用这些功能，但Fly.io通过Macaroon在基础设施上获得了一些 unexpected 的好处。

Fly.io创建了一个名为tkdb的简单系统来管理Macaroon令牌数据，使用LiteFS和Litestream进行SQLite数据库的分布式管理和备份。tkdb运行在独立的硬件上，数据经过加密，具有次秒级复制和时间点恢复功能。由于Macaroon的设计，tkdb数据库非常小且易于管理，写入操作相对简单且少。

尽管与平台其他部分的通信较为复杂，但通过NATS消息系统进行交互得以实现。总体而言，Macaroon系统为Fly.io提供了稳定且安全的令牌管理解决方案。

Weâre Fly.io, a security bearer token company with a public cloud problem. You can read more about what our platform does (Docker container goes in, virtual machine in Singapore comes out), but this is just an engineering deep-dive into how we make our security tokens work. Itâs a tokens nerd post.
1
Weâve spent
too much time
talking about
security tokens
, and about
Macaroon tokens
in particular
. Writing another Macaroon treatise was not on my calendar. But weâre in the process of handing off our internal Macaroon project to a new internal owner, and in the process of truing up our operations manuals for these systems, I found myself in the position of writing a giant post about them. So, why not share?
Can I sum up Macaroons in a short paragraph? Macaroon tokens are bearer tokens (like JWTs) that use a cute chained-HMAC construction that allows an end-user to take any existing token they have and scope it down, all on their own. You can minimize your token before every API operation so that youâre only ever transmitting the least amount of privilege needed for what youâre actually doing, even if the token you were issued was an admin token. And they have a user-serviceable plug-in interface!
Youâll have to read the earlier post to learn more about that
.
Yes, probably, we are.
A couple years in to being the Internetâs largest user of Macaroons, I can report (as many predicted) that for our users, the cool things about Macaroons are a mixed bag in practice. Itâs very neat that users can edit their own tokens, or even email them to partners without worrying too much. But users donât really take advantage of token features.
But Iâm still happy we did this, because Macaroon quirks have given us a bunch of unexpected wins in our infrastructure. Our internal token system has turned out to be one of the nicer parts of our platform. Hereâs why.
2
As an operator, the most important thing to know about Macaroons is that theyâre online-stateful; you need a database somewhere. A Macaroon token starts with a random field (a nonce) and the first thing you do when verifying a token is to look that nonce up in a database. So one of the most important details of a Macaroon implementation is where that database lives.
I can tell you one place weâre not OK with it living: in our primary API cluster.
Thereâs several reasons for that. Some of them are about scalability and reliability: far and away the most common failure mode of an outage on our platform is âdeploys are brokenâ, and those failures are usually caused by API instability. It would not be OK if âdeploys are brokenâ transitively meant âdeployed apps canât use security tokensâ. But the biggest reason is security: root secrets for Macaroon tokens are hazmat, and a basic rule of thumb in secure design is: keep hazmat away from complicated code.
So we created a deliberately simple system to manage token data. Itâs called
tkdb
.
LiteFS: primary/replica distributed SQLite; Litestream: PITR SQLite replication to object storage; both work with unmodified SQLite libraries.
tkdb
is about 5000 lines of Go code that manages a SQLite database that is in turn managed by
LiteFS
and
Litestream
. It runs on isolated hardware (in the US, Europe, and Australia) and records in the database are encrypted with an injected secret. LiteFS gives us subsecond replication from our US primary to EU and AU, allows us to shift the primary to a different region, and gives us point-in-time recovery of the database.
Weâve been running Macaroons for a couple years now, and the entire
tkdb
database is just a couple dozen megs large. Most of that data isnât real. A full PITR recovery of the database takes just seconds. We use SQLite for a lot of our infrastructure, and this is one of the very few well-behaved databases we have.
Thatâs in large part a consequence of the design of Macaroons. Thereâs actually not much for us to store! The most complicated possible Macaroon still chains up to a single root key (we generate a key per Fly.io âorganizationâ; you don’t share keys with your neighbors), and everything that complicates that Macaroon happens âofflineâ. We take advantage of  “attenuation” far more than our users do.
The result is that database writes are relatively rare and very simple: we just need to record an HMAC key when Fly.io organizations are created (that is, roughly, when people sign up for the service and actually do a deploy). That, and revocation lists (more on that later), which make up most of the data.
3
Talking to
tkdb
from the rest of our platform is complicated, for historical reasons.
NATS is fine, we just donât really need it.
Ben Toews is responsible for most of the good things about this implementation. When he inherited the v0 Macaroons code from me, we were in the middle of a weird love affair with
NATS
, the messaging system. So

主要讨论点：前FCC主席因其任职期间的行为而获得奖励，这种行为模式是否合理

不同观点：
• **[sc68cal的观点]**：前FCC主席因为在其任期内迎合行业而获得奖励，这是一种既定的模式。他指出，作为行业监管者，有人在任期内迎合行业，并期望在任期结束后得到回报，这种现象很常见。这暗示了对监管者可能与行业之间存在利益输送或旋转门问题的批评。

• **[lioeters的观点]**：在正常国家，这种行为应被视为犯罪。他认为，这种监管者在任期内迎合行业、离任后获得回报的行为是不道德的，甚至应受到法律制裁。这反映了对监管和行业之间不当关系的严厉批评。

• **[muro的观点]**：对未来可能出现的更极端情况表示讽刺，提到未来可能会出现同时兼任监管者和行业职位的情况。这暗示了对监管机构与行业之间边界模糊的担忧，并通过讽刺表达对这种趋势的反对。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：这种监管者在任期内迎合行业、离任后获得回报的行为是否应该被视为腐败或不当行为。sc68cal和lioeters认为这是一种不正当的行为模式，而muro则通过讽刺表达了对未来可能出现的更严重问题的担忧。

• **论据和例子**：sc68cal提到了这是一种既定的模式，暗示这种现象的普遍性。lioeters则认为在正常国家这种行为应被视为犯罪，强调其不道德性和潜在的违法性。muro通过讽刺表达了对未来可能出现的更极端情况的不满和担忧。

• **讨论关系**：sc68cal和lioeters的观点相似，都批评了这种行为模式，而muro的观点则在此基础上进一步讽刺和担忧未来可能出现的更严重问题。

data.title: US Govt is upselling AWS as a PaaS?
data.author: besus
data.article_summary: Cloud.gov 提供不同层级的云服务购买选项，用户通过购买相应等级的 credits 来获取服务，这些 credits 可用于应用程序内存或托管云服务（如数据库）。此外，还提供价格为 250 美元/小时的专业服务。各层级价格从免费的 Sandbox 到最高 2000 credits 的 Giga（936,000 美元）不等。每个 credit 的价格为 50 美元，每 GB 内存需要 3 个 credits。定价包含 FedRAMP 合规、资源指导、客户和社区支持、持续安全合规以及单点登录功能。企业客户可联系 cloud.gov 了解折扣和中介服务定价。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于公共部门云服务价格和集中化PaaS平台的讨论

不同观点：
• **greatgib**：认为公共部门在云服务上被过度收费，1GB内存收费150美元，一小时专业服务收费250美元，这显得公共部门被严重宰割。
• **bberenberg**：指出云服务文档（https://cloud.gov/docs/overview/what-is-cloudgov/）是关键，认为政府正试图建立一个集中化的PaaS平台来统一处理政府内的云服务工作。他对这一做法是否比当前承包商提供的GovCloud更具成本效益持观望态度。
• **Rastonbury**：认为集中化合同和标准化设置的理论是好的，可以减少每个部门单独谈判的麻烦，并获得更优惠的价格。但在实际执行中，如何定价以及如何在不同预算间分摊成本是挑战。
• **throw03172019**：以讽刺的语气提到这是否是Elon的“Giga”云，暗示对高价和效率的怀疑。
• **besus**：认为价格表不合理，询问其他人是否有相关经验，对价格的合理性提出质疑。
• **verdverm**：引用“像企业一样运营政府”的说法，讽刺地指出这种做法可能会导致剥削，直到政府加以制止。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于公共部门云服务的价格是否合理以及集中化平台的可行性和执行难度。
- 不同评论者对价格的看法存在明显分歧，部分人认为价格过高（greatgib, besus, verdverm），而其他人则关注集中化平台的潜在优势和执行挑战（bberenberg, Rastonbury）。
- 讽刺和幽默（throw03172019, verdverm）被用来表达对高价和效率的怀疑。

Elektron MCP
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows Claude and other MCP-compatible LLMs to interact with and control Elektron synthesizers via MIDI.
Prompt examples
“Use Digitone MCP to design an evolving dark pad using the Wavetone machine on track 1.”
"Use Digitone MPC to design a Dark thick pad using Wavetone machine on track 1."
Only Wavetone machine is supported for now, other machines will be added soon, stay tuned!
Features
Complete MIDI control interface for the Elektron Digitone synthesizer
Structured controllers for all Digitone sound engines:
Wavetone (waveshaping synthesis)
FM Tone (FM synthesis)
FM Drum (percussive FM synthesis)
Swarmer (unison/swarm synthesis)
Comprehensive parameter control for:
All filter types
MultiMode
Lowpass4
Equalizer
LegacyLpHp
CombMinus
CombPlus
BaseWidth
Amplitude and envelope settings
Effects processing (delay, reverb, chorus, bit reduction, etc.)
LFOs control
MCP server exposing all synth parameters as tools for LLMs
Type-safe parameter validation using Pydantic
Modular architecture for easy extension to other Elektron devices
Demo
Watch Claude control the Elektron Digitone synthesizer in real-time:
Installation and Usage
Prerequisites
Python 3.10+
uv
for package management
An Elektron Digitone connected via USB
Claude Desktop app (for full integration)
Installing Dependencies
uv is mandatory for this project so start by installing it:
For macOS:
brew install uv
For Windows:
Follow the instructions
here
3. Installing with Claude Desktop
To use with Claude AI, add the MCP server configuration in Claude Desktop:
⚠️
Important
: You don't need to clone the repository or install the packages, all you need is to add the MCP server configuration to your claude_desktop_config.json file the MPC server is already published on pypi.
Go to Claude > Settings > Developer > Edit Config > claude_desktop_config.json to include the following:
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"Digitone 2"
: {
"command"
:
"
uvx
"
,
"args"
: [
"
elektron-mcp
"
]
}
}
}
Architecture
The library is designed with a clean, object-oriented architecture:
Base Controllers
: Common functionality abstracted into base classes
Specialized Controllers
: Dedicated controllers for each synth engine and module
MCP Tools
: Direct interface between LLMs and the synth's parameters
MIDI Interface
: Reliable communication with Digitone hardware
Implementation Details
This library uses:
FastMCP
: For exposing synth controls to LLMs
Pydantic models
: For data validation, serialization, and type safety
mido
: For MIDI communication
Use Cases
Allow Claude and other LLMs to create and modify sounds on the Digitone
Programmatically control Digitone parameters for automated sound design
Bridge between AI-generated music and hardware synthesis
Future Extensions
Support for additional Elektron devices (Analog Four, Octatrack, etc.)
Pattern sequencing and automation
Sound preset management
Additional synthesis parameters

Reporting by Emily Fishbein was supported by the Pulitzer Center.
Heading north in the dark, the only way Gavesh could try to track his progress through the Thai countryside was by watching the road signs zip by. The Jeep’s three occupants—Gavesh, a driver, and a young Chinese woman—had no languages in common, so they drove for hours in nervous silence as they wove their way out of Bangkok and toward Mae Sot, a city on Thailand’s western border with Myanmar.
When they reached the city, the driver pulled off the road toward a small hotel, where another car was waiting. “I had some suspicions—like, why are we changing vehicles?” Gavesh remembers. “But it happened so fast.”
They left the highway and drove on until, in total darkness, they parked at what looked like a private house. “We stopped the vehicle. There were people gathered. Maybe 10 of them. They took the luggage and they asked us to come,” Gavesh says. “One was going in front, there was another one behind, and everyone said: ‘Go, go, go.’”
Gavesh and the Chinese woman were marched through the pitch-black fields by flashlight to a riverside where a boat was moored. By then, it was far too late to back out.
Gavesh’s journey had started, seemingly innocently, with a job ad on Facebook promising work he desperately needed.
Instead, he found himself trafficked into a business commonly known as “pig butchering”—a form of fraud in which scammers form romantic or other close relationships with targets online and extract money from them. The Chinese crime syndicates behind the scams have netted billions of dollars, and they have used violence and coercion to force their workers, many of them people trafficked like Gavesh, to carry out the frauds from large compounds, several of which operate openly in the quasi-lawless borderlands of Myanmar.
We spoke to Gavesh and five other workers from inside the scam industry, as well as anti-trafficking experts and technology specialists. Their testimony reveals how global companies, including American social media and dating apps and international cryptocurrency and messaging platforms, have given the fraud business the means to become industrialized. By the same token, it is Big Tech that may hold the key to breaking up the scam syndicates—if only these companies can be persuaded or compelled to act.
We’re identifying Gavesh using a pseudonym to protect his identity. He is from a country in South Asia, one he asked us not to name. He hasn’t shared his story much, and he still hasn’t told his family. He worries about how they’d handle it.
Until the pandemic, he had held down a job in the tourism industry. But lockdowns had gutted the sector, and two years later he was working as a day laborer to support himself and his father and sister. “I was fed up with my life,” he says. “I was trying so hard to find a way to get out.”
Related Story
Artificial intelligence is creating a new colonial world order
An MIT Technology Review series investigates how AI is enriching a powerful few by dispossessing communities that have been dispossessed before.
When he saw the Facebook post in mid-2022, it seemed like a godsend. A company in Thailand was looking for English-speaking customer service and data entry specialists. The monthly salary was $1,500—far more than he could earn at home—with meals, travel costs, a visa, and accommodation included. “I knew if I got this job, my life would turn around. I would be able to give my family a good life,” Gavesh says.
What came next was life-changing, but not in the way Gavesh had hoped. The advert was a fraud—and a classic tactic syndicates use to force workers like Gavesh into an economy that operates as something like a dark mirror of the global outsourcing industry.
The true scale of this type of fraud is hard to estimate, but the United Nations
reported
in 2023 that hundreds of thousands of people had been trafficked to work as online scammers in Southeast Asia. One 2024 study, from the University of Texas, estimates that the criminal syndicates that run these businesses have
stolen at least $75 billion
since 2020.
These schemes have been going on for more than two decades, but they’ve started to capture global attention only recently, as the syndicates running them increasingly
shift
from Chinese targets toward the West. And even as investigators, international organizations, and journalists gradually pull back the curtain on the brutal conditions inside scamming compounds and document their vast scale, what is far less exposed is the pivotal role platforms owned by Big Tech play throughout the industry—from initially coercing individuals to become scammers to, finally, duping scam targets out of their life savings.

looked for ways

• 观点二：补贴机制有利于电力公司股东，而非普通消费者。自2017年以来，俄亥俄州居民已经为OVEC的电厂补贴支付了近6亿美元，预计到2030年总补贴金额将超过10亿美元，这些资金直接流向电力公司的股东，增加了他们的利润。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在AI时代设计有效的技术面试

不同观点：
• **muzani的观点**：
  - Leetcode风格的题目已经不再有效，因为AI能在短时间内解决这些问题。
  - 主张使用限时较短的回家作业（如4小时内完成的Wordle克隆），以评估候选人的综合能力，包括使用库、架构设计、技术栈选择、提交记录等。
  - 认为面试题目应区分AI用户和非AI用户，并测试候选人的实际工程能力。
  
• **austin-cheney的观点**：
  - 认为AI带来的问题只存在于不擅长面试的考官身上。
  - 主张使用开放式问题，要求候选人提供精确的答案，例如讨论他们最喜欢的Node库的方法，或解释全双工通信等概念。
  - 认为只要面试官设计得当，AI不会成为问题。

• **nextts的观点**：
  - 简短列出候选人，链接了一个招聘页面，未展开具体论述。

• **scarface_74的观点**：
  - 认为如果AI能通过面试但不能胜任工作，说明面试流程本身有问题。
  - 主张面试应该直接评估候选人的实际工作能力，而不是可以通过AI轻松解决的问题。

• **paulcole的观点**：
  - 认为即使候选人使用AI通过面试，只要他们能完成工作就可以。
  - 强调如果候选人不能胜任工作，无论是否使用AI，都会被解雇。
  - 认为使用AI通过面试并无不道德之处。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：AI在技术面试中的作用和影响。一部分人认为AI使得传统的技术面试题失效，需要重新设计面试流程；另一部分人则认为只要面试设计得当，AI不会成为问题。
- **面试设计**：muzani强调回家作业和实际工程能力的评估，austin-cheney则强调开放式问题和精确答案。
- **AI的伦理问题**：paulcole认为使用AI通过面试并无不道德，而scarface_74则认为面试应该直接评估实际工作能力。

这些观点反映了在AI时代，技术面试设计中的不同思路和关注点。

data.title: Waymos crash less than human drivers
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Waymo自动驾驶汽车的安全记录。在超过5000万英里的驾驶中，Waymo报告了约60起严重碰撞事故，但大多数事故是由于人类司机违反交通规则造成的，比如超速、闯红灯等。文章提到，2025年1月在旧金山发生了一起致命事故，虽然涉及Waymo车辆，但责任在于人类司机。在2024年7月至2025年2月期间，Waymo报告了38起较为严重的事故，其中仅一起明确是Waymo的责任。总体来看，Waymo的碰撞率远低于人类司机，显示出其自动驾驶技术在安全性上的优势，但随着其服务扩展，未来可能仍会涉及更多事故。文章强调，在评估自动驾驶安全性时，应考虑整体行驶里程和事故发生率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Waymo及其他自动驾驶汽车的安全性与实际应用效果

不同观点：
• [wnissen] 认为Waymo在技术上表现出色，尤其在与人类司机的严重事故对比中占优。他引用数据说明20%的司机导致了80%的事故，且对Waymo能否盈利更感兴趣。
• [labrador] 对Waymo使用多种技术（视觉提示、激光雷达、地理围栏等）保障安全表示认可，但对特斯拉仅依赖视觉提示表示不信任，尤其提到特斯拉在面对 painted wall 时的潜在问题。
• [hmmm-i-wonder] 质疑仅用事故作为衡量自动驾驶成功的标准，指出许多不良驾驶行为（如危险决策、交通混乱）不会直接导致事故，但依然危险。
• [mjburgess] 关注自动驾驶汽车在不同环境中的泛化能力及潜在的系统性故障风险，认为广泛应用可能导致意外的大规模事故。他还质疑Waymo提供数据的统计有效性。
• [ikerino] 对Waymo事故率的微小变化提出质疑，认为用词可能有误导性，建议应更明确说明数据是否真的变差。
• [1970-01-01] 指出Waymo的数据主要来自天气良好的城市，缺乏在恶劣天气条件下的对比，认为应在多变环境下测试。
• [myflash13] 对Waymo和特斯拉的安全声明持怀疑态度，指出可能存在数据操纵，包括提前脱离自动驾驶、选择简单路线等问题，建议公开所有原始数据。
• [paxys] 认为自动驾驶仅比“平均”人类司机好是不够的，应该与“理智且有经验的司机”对比，否则替代80%好司机可能导致整体事故率上升。
• [devit] 提出自动驾驶是否能像人类司机一样激进驾驶的问题，列举多种可能的激进驾驶行为，认为这些行为虽然增加风险，但也能提高速度和效率。
• [ra7] 提供Waymo安全数据的详细链接，鼓励查看更全面的比较方法。
• [slifin] 用渡轮与 Jet Ski 的类比，质疑大量自动驾驶汽车上路是否合理，认为可能导致交通堵塞和能源浪费，建议公共交通更为有效。
• [JKCalhoun] 认为每个人拥有自动驾驶汽车的未来缺乏远见，提出公交车可能更安全。
• [nickvec] 对自动驾驶的未来表示乐观，认为能拯救许多生命。
• [jedbrooke] 提到Waymo总是使用转向灯，认为这在安全性上已经优于大部分人类司机。
• [_zamorano_] 提出在欧洲一些复杂交通情况下（如交叉路口让行）自动驾驶系统如何处理的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Waymo及其他自动驾驶汽车是否真的比人类司机更安全，特别是在不同环境和条件下的表现。
• 数据的透明性和统计有效性受到质疑，部分评论者要求更全面和公开的数据分析。
• 自动驾驶是否应模仿人类司机的激进驾驶行为以提高效率，或者是否应以更保守的方式驾驶，也是讨论的重点之一。
• 自动驾驶汽车大规模应用对交通系统和能源的潜在影响也被提及。
